title.zh: 卷三百二十八 列傳第八十七 李清臣 安燾 張璪 蒲宗孟 黃履 蔡挺 王韶 薛向 章楶
title.en: Volume 328 Biographies 87: Li Qingchen, An Dao, Zhang Zao, Pu Zongmeng, Huang Lu, Cai Ting, Wang Shao, Xue Xiang, Zhang Jie
title.raw: 卷三百二十八 列傳第八十七 李清臣 安燾 張璪 蒲宗孟 黃履 蔡挺 王韶 薛向 章楶 Volume 328 Biographies 87: Li Qingchen, An Dao, Zhang Zao, Pu Zongmeng, Huang Lu, Cai Ting, Wang Shao, Xue Xiang, Zhang Jie

sentences.zh: 李清臣

translations.literal: Li Qingchen
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingchen

sentences.zh: 李清臣，字邦直，魏人也。

translations.literal: Li Qingchen, styled Bangzhi, was a man of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingchen, styled Bangzhi, was a native of Wei.

sentences.zh: 七歲知讀書，日數千言，暫經目輒誦，稍能戲為文章。

translations.literal: At seven he knew how to read; each day he read several thousand characters; after a brief glance he could recite them; he could even casually compose essays.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he learned to read. Each day he could read several thousand characters; after a brief look he could recite them from memory, and he could even compose essays for amusement.

sentences.zh: 客有從京師來者，與其兄談佛寺火，清臣從傍應曰：「此所謂災也，或者其蠹民已甚，天固儆之邪？」

translations.literal: A guest who had come from the capital was discussing with his elder brother a fire at a Buddhist temple. Qingchen responded from the side, saying: "This is what is called a calamity. Perhaps the people have been exploited too severely, and Heaven is warning them?"
translations.idiomatic: A visitor who had come from the capital was talking with his elder brother about a fire at a Buddhist temple. Qingchen chimed in from the side: "This is what people call a calamity. Perhaps the temples have preyed on the people too long, and Heaven is sending a warning?"

sentences.zh: 因作《浮圖災解》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote 《An Explanation of the Buddhist Temple Calamity》.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wrote 《An Explanation of the Buddhist Temple Calamity》.

sentences.zh: 兄驚曰：「是必大吾門。」

translations.literal: His brother said in astonishment: "He will surely greatly enlarge our family."
translations.idiomatic: His brother exclaimed in amazement: "He is sure to bring great honor to our house."

sentences.zh: 韓琦聞其名，以兄之子妻之。

translations.literal: When Han Qi heard of his fame, he gave him his nephew's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi heard of his reputation, he gave him his nephew's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調邢州司戶參軍、和川令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Registrar of the Revenue Section in Xingzhou and Magistrate of Hechuan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed revenue registrar in Xingzhou and magistrate of Hechuan.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，薦者逾十數，應得京官。

translations.literal: When his term expired, more than ten people recommended him; he was due to receive a capital-office appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, more than ten people recommended him, and he was eligible for promotion to a capital post.

sentences.zh: 適舉將薛向有公事未竟，閡銓格，判銓張掞擿使自陳勿用。

translations.literal: It happened that Xue Xiang, who was to be recommended at the same time, had unfinished official business, which blocked the personnel regulations. Zhang Shan, the personnel judge, singled Qingchen out and had him state that he should not be used.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Xue Xiang, who was also up for recommendation, had unfinished official business that blocked the normal personnel rules. Zhang Shan, the personnel judge, singled out Qingchen and told him to declare that he should withdraw his candidacy.

sentences.zh: 清臣曰：「人以家保己而己舍之，薄矣。

translations.literal: Qingchen said: "Others use their households to protect themselves, yet I would abandon them—that would be mean.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen said: "Others rely on their families to protect themselves, yet I would abandon mine—that would be unworthy.

sentences.zh: 願待之。」

translations.literal: I wish to wait for him."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather wait for him."

sentences.zh: 掞離席曰：「君能如是，未可量也。」

translations.literal: Shan rose from his seat and said: "If you can act like this, your future cannot be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Shan rose from his seat and said: "If you can act like this, there is no telling how far you may go."

sentences.zh: 應材識兼茂科，歐陽修壯其文，以比蘇軾。

translations.literal: He entered the Examinations for Exceptional Talent and Learning, and Ouyang Xiu admired his writing, comparing him to Su Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Examinations for Exceptional Talent and Learning. Ouyang Xiu admired his writing and compared him to Su Shi.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，試秘閣，考官韓維曰：「荀卿氏筆力也。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, he took the Secretariat examination. Examiner Han Wei said: "This is the brushwork of Master Xun."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhiping reign, he took the Secretariat examination. Examiner Han Wei said: "This has the force of Xunzi's pen."

sentences.zh: 試文至中書，修迎語曰：「不置李清臣於第一，則謬矣。」

translations.literal: When the examination essay reached the Secretariat, Xiu greeted them and said: "If Li Qingchen is not placed first, it will be an error."
translations.idiomatic: When the examination essay reached the Secretariat, Ouyang Xiu met them and said: "If Li Qingchen is not placed first, the grading will be wrong."

sentences.zh: 啟視如言。

translations.literal: When they opened and looked, it was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: When they opened the papers and looked, it was exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 時大雨霖，災異數見，論者歸咎濮議。

translations.literal: At that time heavy rains continued for a long time, and strange omens appeared repeatedly; many commentators blamed the dispute over the title of Emperor Yingzong's biological father.
translations.idiomatic: At that time prolonged rains fell and strange omens appeared again and again; many commentators blamed the dispute over the posthumous title of Emperor Yingzong's biological father.

sentences.zh: 及廷對，或謂曰：「宜以《五行傳》『簡宗廟，水不潤下』為證，必擢上第。」

translations.literal: When it came to the palace examination, someone told him: "You should use as evidence from the 《Treatise on the Five Phases》 the passage 'When ancestral temples are neglected, water does not descend to moisten below'—you will surely be promoted to the top rank."
translations.idiomatic: When the palace examination came, someone told him: "You should cite the 《Treatise on the Five Phases》—'When ancestral temples are neglected, water does not descend'—as your evidence. You are sure to win the top rank."

sentences.zh: 清臣曰：「此漢儒附會之說也，吾不之信。

translations.literal: Qingchen said: "This is a forced interpretation by Han Confucians; I do not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen said: "That is a forced interpretation by Han-dynasty Confucians. I do not believe it.

sentences.zh: 民間豈無疾痛可上者乎？」

translations.literal: Are there not sufferings among the people that can be reported upward?"
translations.idiomatic: Are there not sufferings among the people that ought to be reported to the throne?"

sentences.zh: 即條對言：「天地之大，譬如人一身，腹心肺腑有所攻塞，則五官為之不寧。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a detailed response, saying: "Heaven and Earth are vast, like a single human body: when the belly, heart, lungs, and viscera suffer obstruction, then the five senses are disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a detailed response: "Heaven and Earth are vast, like a single human body. When the belly, heart, lungs, and inner organs are blocked, the five senses are thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 民人生聚，天地之腹心肺腑也；

translations.literal: The gathering and multiplication of the people are the belly, heart, lungs, and viscera of Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: The people who live and multiply upon the earth are the belly, heart, lungs, and inner organs of Heaven and Earth;

sentences.zh: 日月星辰，天地之五官也。

translations.literal: the sun, moon, and stars are the five senses of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: the sun, moon, and stars are the five senses of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 善止天地之異者，不止其異，止民之疾痛而已。」

translations.literal: One who skillfully stops the anomalies of Heaven and Earth does not merely stop the anomalies; he stops only the sufferings of the people."
translations.idiomatic: To stop Heaven and Earth's anomalies properly is not to stop the anomalies themselves, but to relieve the people's suffering."

sentences.zh: 策入等，以秘書郎簽書平江軍判官，名聲籍甚。

translations.literal: His policy essay was graded in the top class. He was appointed Secretary and Acting Military Administrator of Pingjiang, and his fame spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: His policy essay was graded in the top class. He was appointed secretary and acting military administrator of Pingjiang, and his reputation spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 英宗知之，語王廣淵曰：「韓琦固忠臣，但避嫌太審。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong knew of him and said to Wang Guangyuan: "Han Qi is indeed a loyal minister, but he is too cautious in avoiding suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong learned of him and said to Wang Guangyuan: "Han Qi is certainly a loyal minister, but he is overly cautious about avoiding suspicion.

sentences.zh: 如李清臣者，公議皆謂可用，顧以親抑之可乎？」

translations.literal: As for someone like Li Qingchen, public opinion all says he can be used—yet is it right to suppress him because of kinship?"
translations.idiomatic: As for someone like Li Qingchen, public opinion holds that he should be employed. Is it right to hold him back merely because of family ties?"

sentences.zh: 既而詔舉館閣，歐陽修薦之，得集賢校理、同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict called for recommendations to the Hanlin and Archive posts. Ouyang Xiu recommended him, and he received the posts of Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward an edict called for recommendations to the Hanlin and archive posts. Ouyang Xiu recommended him, and he was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 從韓絳使陝西。

translations.literal: He followed Han Jiang on a mission to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Han Jiang on a mission to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 慶卒亂，家屬九指揮應誅，清臣請於絳，配隸為奴婢。

translations.literal: When Qing soldiers mutinied, nine commanders among the families deserved execution. Qingchen appealed to Jiang to assign them as bonded servants instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing soldiers mutinied, nine commanders among the families deserved execution. Qingchen pleaded with Han Jiang to assign them as bonded servants instead.

sentences.zh: 絳坐貶，清臣亦通判海州。

translations.literal: Jiang was demoted for this, and Qingchen too was made vice-prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang was demoted for this, and Qingchen too was made vice-prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，還故官，出提點京東刑獄。

translations.literal: After a long time he returned to his former post and went out as judicial intendant of Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he returned to his former post and was sent out as judicial intendant of Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 齊、魯盜賊為天下劇，設耳目方略，名捕且盡。

translations.literal: Bandits in Qi and Lu were the worst in the realm; he set up informants and stratagems, and captured nearly all those sought by name.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Qi and Lu were the worst in the realm. He set up informants and stratagems and captured nearly all those sought by name.

sentences.zh: 作韓琦《行狀》，神宗讀之曰：「良史才也。」

translations.literal: He wrote Han Qi's funeral biography. Shenzong read it and said: "This is the talent of a fine historian."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Han Qi's funeral biography. Shenzong read it and said: "This is the talent of a fine historian."

sentences.zh: 召為兩朝國史編修官，撰《河渠》、《律曆》、《選舉》諸志，文直事詳，人以為不減《史》、《漢》。

translations.literal: He was summoned as compiler of the national history for two reigns and drafted the monographs on Rivers and Canals, Calendar and Measures, and Examination and Selection—his writing was plain and his facts detailed, and people thought it did not fall short of the Records and the History of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as compiler of the national history for two reigns and drafted the monographs on Rivers and Canals, Calendar and Measures, and Examination and Selection. His writing was plain and his facts detailed, and people thought it did not fall short of the Records and the History of Han.

sentences.zh: 同修起居注，進知制誥、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was made co-compiler of the diary, then advanced to drafter of edicts and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was made co-compiler of the diary, then advanced to drafter of edicts and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 元豐新官制，拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Under the new Yuanfeng official system he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under the new Yuanfeng official system he was appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 清臣官右正言，當易承議階，帝曰：「安有尚書而猶承議郎者？」

translations.literal: Qingchen's official rank was Right Remonstrator and should have been changed to Chengyi rank. The emperor said: "How can there be a minister of personnel who is still a Chengyilang?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen's rank was Right Remonstrator and should have been changed to Chengyi rank. The emperor said: "How can there be a minister of personnel who is still a Chengyilang?"

sentences.zh: 乃授朝奉大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted the rank of Court Presented Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was granted the rank of Court Presented Grandee.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，轉左丞。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 時熙、豐法度，一切厘正，清臣固爭之，罷為資政殿學士、知河陽，徙河南、永興。

translations.literal: At that time the Xining and Yuanfeng laws and institutions were being entirely revised and corrected. Qingchen firmly opposed this and was dismissed to become Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and Prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Henan and Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xining and Yuanfeng laws and institutions were being thoroughly revised. Qingchen firmly opposed the changes and was dismissed to academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Henan and Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部尚書，給事中姚勔駁之，改知真定府。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Minister of Personnel, but Supervising Secretary Yao Xun objected, and he was reassigned as Prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as minister of personnel, but Supervising Secretary Yao Xun objected, and he was reassigned as prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 班行有王宗正者，致憾於故帥，使其妻詣使者，告前後饋餉過制，囚繫數百人。

translations.literal: Among the officials was one Wang Zongzheng, who bore a grudge against the former prefect. He had his wife go to the investigating commissioner and report that gifts and supplies before and after had exceeded regulations, and several hundred people were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Among the officials was one Wang Zongzheng, who bore a grudge against the former prefect. He had his wife go to the investigating commissioner and report that gifts and supplies had exceeded regulations, and several hundred people were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 清臣至，立奏解其獄，而竄宗正。

translations.literal: When Qingchen arrived, he immediately memorialized to release the prisoners and had Zongzheng banished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingchen arrived, he immediately memorialized to release the prisoners and had Zongzheng banished.

sentences.zh: 帝親政，拜中書侍郎，勔復駁之，不聽。

translations.literal: When the Emperor personally took up government, Qingchen was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat. Xun again objected, but the Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally took up the reins of government, Qingchen was appointed vice director of the Secretariat. Yao Xun objected again, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，廷試進士，清臣發策曰：「今復詞賦之選而士不知勸，罷常平之官而農不加富，可差可募之說雜而役法病，或東或北之論異而河患滋，賜土以柔遠也而羌夷之患未弭，弛利以便民也而商賈之路不通。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, at the palace examination for jinshi graduates, Qingchen issued the examination question, saying: "Now the selection by rhapsody and fu has been restored, yet scholars are not encouraged; the Ever-Normal Granary offices have been abolished, yet farmers are not richer; theories of corvée labor and of hired service are mixed together and the labor-service law is afflicted; theories of going east or going north differ and river disasters grow worse; land was granted to appease distant peoples, yet the troubles of the Qiang and barbarians are not pacified; profits were relaxed to benefit the people, yet the routes of merchants are not open.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaosheng, at the palace examination for jinshi graduates, Qingchen issued the examination question: "The selection by rhapsody and fu has been restored, yet scholars are not encouraged to study. The Ever-Normal Granary offices have been abolished, yet farmers are no richer. Theories of corvée labor and hired service are mixed together, and the labor-service law is in disorder. Debates over going east or north differ, and river disasters grow worse. Land was granted to appease distant peoples, yet the troubles of the Qiang and other tribes are not pacified. Profits were relaxed to benefit the people, yet merchants' routes remain blocked.

sentences.zh: 夫可則因，否則革，惟當之為貴，聖人亦何有必焉。」

translations.literal: What may be followed should be continued; what may not should be reformed. Only what is fitting is precious—even a sage has nothing he must insist upon."
translations.idiomatic: What may be followed should be kept; what may not should be changed. Only what is fitting matters—even a sage has nothing he must insist upon."

sentences.zh: 主意皆絀元祐之政，策士悟其指，於是紹述之論大興，國是遂變。

translations.literal: The intent was entirely to reject the Yuanyou policies. The examination candidates grasped his meaning, and thereafter the theory of continuing the earlier reforms flourished greatly, and the national policy was thereby changed.
translations.idiomatic: The intent was entirely to reject the Yuanyou policies. The candidates grasped his meaning, and the theory of continuing the earlier reforms flourished. The national policy was thereby changed.

sentences.zh: 范純仁去位，清臣獨顓中書，亟復青苗、免役法，除諸路提舉官。

translations.literal: When Fan Chunren left office, Qingchen alone controlled the Secretariat. He quickly restored the Green Sprouts and Exemption-from-Labor laws and appointed promotion commissioners in each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Chunren left office, Qingchen alone controlled the Secretariat. He quickly restored the Green Sprouts and Exemption-from-Labor laws and appointed promotion commissioners in each circuit.

sentences.zh: 覬為相，顧蘇轍軋己，乃擿轍嘗以漢武比先帝激上怒，轍罷。

translations.literal: He coveted the chancellorship, but Su Zhe obstructed him. He therefore picked out that Zhe had once compared the late emperor to Emperor Wu of Han, arousing the Emperor's anger, and Zhe was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He coveted the chancellorship, but Su Zhe stood in his way. He therefore seized on the fact that Zhe had once compared the late emperor to Emperor Wu of Han, arousing the emperor's anger, and Zhe was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時召章惇未至，清臣心益覬之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Dun had been summoned but had not yet arrived; Qingchen's hopes grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Dun had been summoned but had not yet arrived, and Qingchen's hopes grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 已而惇入相，復與為異。

translations.literal: Before long Dun entered the chancellorship, and they again differed from each other.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhang Dun entered the chancellorship, and they again found themselves at odds.

sentences.zh: 惇既逐諸臣，並籍文彥博、呂公著以下三十人，將悉竄嶺表。

translations.literal: After Dun had driven out the various ministers, he also registered Wen Yanbo, Lü Gongzhu, and thirty others below them, intending to banish them all to the region south of the Five Ridges.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Dun had driven out the various ministers, he also registered Wen Yanbo, Lü Gongzhu, and thirty others, intending to banish them all to the far south.

sentences.zh: 清臣曰：「更先帝法度，不為無過，然皆累朝元老，若從惇言，必大駭物聽。」

translations.literal: Qingchen said: "To change the late emperor's laws and institutions was not without fault, yet they are all elders of many reigns. If we follow Dun's words, we will surely greatly shock public opinion."
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen said: "Changing the late emperor's laws and institutions was not without fault, yet these men are elders of many reigns. If we follow Zhang Dun's proposal, we will surely shock public opinion."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是豈無中道耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Is there not a middle course?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Is there not a middle course?

sentences.zh: 合揭榜朝堂，置餘人不問。」

translations.literal: Let us post the list in the court hall and leave the rest unmentioned."
translations.idiomatic: Let us post the list in the court hall and leave the rest alone."

sentences.zh: 鄜延路金明砦主將張興戰沒，惇怒，議盡戮全軍四千人。

translations.literal: In the circuit of Fuyan, the commander Zhang Xing of Jinming Stockade was killed in battle. Dun was angry and proposed executing the entire army of four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the Fuyan circuit, Commander Zhang Xing of Jinming Stockade was killed in battle. Zhang Dun was furious and proposed executing the entire army of four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 清臣曰：「將死亦多端，或先登爭利，或輕身入敵。

translations.literal: Qingchen said: "Generals die in many ways—some charge first to seize advantage, some lightly throw themselves into the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen said: "Generals die in many ways—some charge first to seize advantage, some throw themselves recklessly into the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今悉誅吏士，異時亡將必舉軍降虜矣。」

translations.literal: If we now execute all the officers and soldiers, in future when a general is lost the whole army will surely surrender to the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: If we now execute all the officers and soldiers, then in future when a general falls the whole army will surely surrender to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 於是但誅牙兵十六輩。

translations.literal: Thereupon only sixteen sergeants were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon only sixteen sergeants were executed.

sentences.zh: 上幸楚王第，有狂婦人遮道叫呼，告清臣謀反，屬吏捕治，本澶州娼而為清臣姑子田氏外婦者。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited the residence of the Prince of Chu, a mad woman blocked the road and shouted, accusing Qingchen of plotting rebellion. The officials under authority arrested and investigated her. She had originally been a prostitute in Dazhou and was the outside wife of Qingchen's nephew by marriage, the Tian family.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the residence of the Prince of Chu, a madwoman blocked the road and shouted, accusing Qingchen of plotting rebellion. The officials arrested and investigated her. She had originally been a prostitute in Dazhou and was the mistress of Qingchen's nephew by marriage in the Tian family.

sentences.zh: 清臣不能引去，用御史言，以大學士知河南，尋落職知真定府。

translations.literal: Qingchen could not withdraw on his own. Following the censor's advice, he was made Grand Academician and Prefect of Henan; shortly afterward he was demoted to Prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen could not bring himself to resign. Following the censor's advice, he was made grand academician and prefect of Henan; shortly afterward he was demoted to prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 初，蔡確子渭上書訴父冤，造奇譖以陷劉摯罪，清臣心知其誣，弗之省，坐奪學士。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cai Que's son Wei had submitted a memorial appealing his father's injustice and fabricated strange slanders to trap Liu Zhi in guilt. Qingchen knew in his heart that it was false but did not investigate, and on that account was deprived of his academician title.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cai Que's son Wei had submitted a memorial appealing his father's injustice and fabricated strange slanders to trap Liu Zhi. Qingchen knew in his heart that it was false but did not investigate, and on that account was deprived of his academician title.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，入為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Qingchen entered office as Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Qingchen entered office as vice director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 僕射韓忠彥與之有連，惟其言是聽，出范純禮、張舜民，不使呂希純、劉安世入朝，皆其謀也。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Han Zhongyan was connected with him and listened only to his words. He had Fan Chunli and Zhang Shunmin removed from office and would not allow Lü Xichun and Liu Anshi to enter court—all were his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Han Zhongyan was connected with him and listened only to his counsel. He had Fan Chunli and Zhang Shunmin removed from office and blocked Lü Xichun and Liu Anshi from entering court—all were his schemes.

sentences.zh: 尋為曾布所陷，出知大名府而卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: Before long he was trapped by Zeng Bu, was sent out as Prefect of Daming, and died there at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was trapped by Zeng Bu, was sent out as prefect of Daming, and died there at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Grandee of the Golden Girdle and Purple Purse.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grandee of the Golden Girdle and Purple Purse.

sentences.zh: 清臣蚤以詞藻受知神宗，建大理寺，築都城，皆命作記，簡重宏放，文體各成一家。

translations.literal: Qingchen early won recognition from Emperor Shenzong for his literary talent. When the Court of Judicial Review was established and the capital walls were built, he was ordered to compose commemorative accounts for both. His style was concise, weighty, and expansive; in each case his literary manner formed a school of its own.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen won early recognition from Emperor Shenzong for his literary talent. When the Court of Judicial Review was established and the capital walls were built, he was ordered to compose commemorative accounts for both. His style was concise, weighty, and expansive; in each case his prose formed a school of its own.

sentences.zh: 為人寬洪，不忮害。

translations.literal: As a man he was broad and magnanimous and did not harbor malice.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was broad-minded and magnanimous and did not harbor malice.

sentences.zh: 嘗為舒亶所劾，及在尚書，亶以贓抵罪，獨申救之，曰：「亶信亡狀，然謂之贓則不可。」

translations.literal: He had once been impeached by Shu Dan. When he was in the Ministry of Personnel, Dan was convicted of embezzlement, but Qingchen alone pleaded for his rescue, saying: "Dan's conduct was indeed deplorable, yet to call it embezzlement is not acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: He had once been impeached by Shu Dan. When he served in the Ministry of Personnel, Dan was convicted of embezzlement, but Qingchen alone pleaded for him, saying: "Dan's conduct was indeed deplorable, yet to call it embezzlement is not acceptable."

sentences.zh: 再為姚勔所駁，當紹聖議貶，或激使甘心，清臣為之言曰：「勔以職事，所見或不同，豈應以臣故而加重？」

translations.literal: He was again opposed by Yao Xun. When the Shaosheng court debated demoting Xun, some urged making him suffer to the full. Qingchen spoke on his behalf, saying: "Xun, in the course of his duties, may see things differently—how can we increase his punishment because of me?"
translations.idiomatic: He was again opposed by Yao Xun. When the Shaosheng court debated demoting Xun, some urged making him suffer to the full. Qingchen spoke on his behalf: "Xun, in the course of his duties, may see things differently—how can we increase his punishment because of me?"

sentences.zh: 帝悟，薄勔罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood and lightened Xun's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and lightened Yao Xun's punishment.

sentences.zh: 起身窮約，以儉自持，至富貴不改。

translations.literal: He rose from poverty and hardship and maintained himself through frugality; even when he reached wealth and honor he did not change.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from poverty and hardship and maintained himself through frugality; even when he reached wealth and honor he did not change.

sentences.zh: 居官奉法，毋敢撓以私。

translations.literal: In office he observed the law and did not dare bend it for private reasons.
translations.idiomatic: In office he observed the law and did not dare bend it for private reasons.

sentences.zh: 然志在利祿，不公於謀國，一意欲取宰相，故操持悖謬，竟不如願以死。

translations.literal: Yet his ambition lay in profit and salary; he was not fair in planning for the state. He was bent solely on becoming chancellor, and therefore his conduct was perverse and mistaken; in the end he did not obtain his wish and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his ambition lay in profit and office; he was not fair-minded in planning for the state. He was bent solely on becoming chancellor, and therefore his conduct was perverse and mistaken. In the end he did not obtain his wish and died.

sentences.zh: 後朝議以復孟后罪，追貶武安軍節度副使，再貶雷州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Later the court debated the crime of restoring Empress Meng and posthumously demoted him to Military Vice Commissioner of Wu'an, then again to Registrar of the Revenue Section in Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court debated the crime of restoring Empress Meng and posthumously demoted him to military vice commissioner of Wu'an, then again to revenue registrar in Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 安燾，字厚卿，開封人。

translations.literal: An Dao, styled Houqing, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: An Dao, styled Houqing, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 幼警悟。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was keen and perceptive.

sentences.zh: 年十一，從學里中，羞與群兒伍，聞有老先生聚徒，往師之。

translations.literal: At eleven he studied in the village school but was ashamed to keep company with the other boys. Hearing that an old master was gathering students, he went to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he studied in the village school but was ashamed to keep company with the other boys. Hearing that an old master was gathering students, he went to study under him.

sentences.zh: 先生曰：「汝方為誦數之學，未可從吾遊，當群試省題一詩，中選乃置汝。」

translations.literal: The master said: "You are still at the stage of recitation and counting studies; you cannot yet follow me in study. The group will test you with a provincial-examination topic poem—if you are selected, then I will take you in."
translations.idiomatic: The master said: "You are still at the stage of rote learning; you cannot yet study with me. The group will test you with a provincial-examination topic poem—if you pass, then I will take you in."

sentences.zh: 燾無難色。

translations.literal: Dao showed no difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Dao showed no hesitation.

sentences.zh: 詩成，出諸生上，由是知名。

translations.literal: When the poem was finished, it ranked above all the other students, and from this he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: When the poem was finished, it ranked above all the other students, and from this he became famous.

sentences.zh: 登第，調蔡州觀察推官，至太常丞、主管大名府路機宜文字。

translations.literal: He passed the examination and was appointed Investigating Commissioner in Caizhou, rising to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Supervisor of Documents for the Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination and was appointed investigating commissioner in Caizhou, rising to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and supervisor of documents for the Daming circuit.

sentences.zh: 用歐陽修薦，為秘閣校理、判吏部南曹、荊湖北路轉運判官、提點刑獄兼常平、農田水利、差役事。

translations.literal: On Ouyang Xiu's recommendation he became Collator in the Secretariat Pavilion, Judge of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, Transport Commissioner of Jinghu North Circuit, and Judicial Intendant concurrently overseeing Ever-Normal Granary, agricultural fields and waterworks, and corvée labor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On Ouyang Xiu's recommendation he became collator in the Secretariat Pavilion, judge of the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, transport commissioner of Jinghu North circuit, and judicial intendant concurrently overseeing Ever-Normal Granary, agricultural fields and waterworks, and corvée labor affairs.

sentences.zh: 時方興新法，奉行之吏，或迎合求進。

translations.literal: At that time the new laws were being launched, and the officials who implemented them sometimes catered to superiors in order to advance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the new laws were being launched, and the officials who implemented them sometimes catered to superiors in order to advance.

sentences.zh: 司農符檄日夜下，如免役增寬剩，造簿供手實，青苗責保任，追胥苛切，其類旁午。

translations.literal: Orders from the Ministry of Revenue came down day and night—such as increasing surplus funds under the exemption-from-labor law, compiling registers and submitting household declarations, requiring guarantors for Green Sprouts loans, and harsh collection by runners—these and similar matters crowded in from all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Orders from the Ministry of Revenue came down day and night—increasing surplus funds under the exemption-from-labor law, compiling registers and submitting household declarations, requiring guarantors for Green Sprouts loans, and harsh collection by runners—such matters crowded in from all sides.

sentences.zh: 燾平心奉法，列其泰甚於朝。

translations.literal: Dao impartially observed the law and listed in court those who went too far.
translations.idiomatic: Dao impartially observed the law and reported to court those who went too far.

sentences.zh: 移使京東路，過闕入見，神宗偉其儀觀，留檢正中書孔目房、修起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred as commissioner to the Jingdong Circuit. Passing through the capital to have an audience, Emperor Shenzong admired his bearing and appearance and kept him as Reviewer in the Secretariat Accounts Office and Compiler of the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as commissioner to the Jingdong circuit. Passing through the capital for an audience, Emperor Shenzong admired his bearing and appearance and kept him as reviewer in the Secretariat accounts office and compiler of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，高麗新通使，假燾左諫議大夫往報之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng, Goryeo newly sent envoys, and Dao was temporarily given the title of Left Remonstrator to go and respond.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanfeng, Goryeo newly sent envoys, and Dao was temporarily given the title of Left Remonstrator to go and respond.

sentences.zh: 高麗迎勞，館餼加契丹禮數等，使近臣言：「王遇使者甚敬，出誠心，非若奉契丹苟免邊患而已。」

translations.literal: Goryeo welcomed and entertained him, adding to the provisions and ritual courtesies equal to those for Khitan envoys. An envoy's close minister said: "Our king treats your envoys with great respect and shows sincere heart—it is not like serving the Khitan merely to avoid border troubles."
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo welcomed and entertained him, adding provisions and ritual courtesies equal to those for Khitan envoys. A close minister of the envoy said: "Our king treats your envoys with great respect and shows sincere heart—it is not like serving the Khitan merely to avoid border troubles."

sentences.zh: 燾笑答曰：「尊中華，事大國，禮一也，特以罕至有加爾。

translations.literal: Dao smiled and replied: "Honoring China and serving a great state—the ritual is one and the same. It is only because you come so rarely that there is something extra.
translations.idiomatic: Dao smiled and replied: "Honoring China and serving a great state—the ritual is one and the same. It is only because you come so rarely that there is something extra.

sentences.zh: 朝廷與遼國通好久，豈復於此較厚薄哉！」

translations.literal: The court has had relations with the Liao state for a long time—how could we still compare thickness and thinness here!"
translations.idiomatic: The court has had relations with the Liao state for a long time—how could we still compare who receives more courtesy here!"

sentences.zh: 使還，帝以為知禮，即授所假官，兼直學士院。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, the Emperor considered him knowledgeable in ritual and immediately granted the title he had been given temporarily, together with appointment in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned, the emperor considered him knowledgeable in ritual and immediately granted the title he had been given temporarily, together with appointment in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 知審刑院，決剖滯訟五百餘案。

translations.literal: As Director of the Court of Judicial Review, he decided and disposed of more than five hundred backlog cases.
translations.idiomatic: As director of the Court of Judicial Review, he decided and disposed of more than five hundred backlog cases.

sentences.zh: 因言：「每蔽獄上省，輕重有疑，則必致駁，勢既不敵，故法官顧避稽停。

translations.literal: He then said: "Whenever a closed case is sent up to the Secretariat, if there is doubt about severity, it is always sent back for reconsideration. Since the power is unequal, judicial officials therefore shrink back and delay.
translations.idiomatic: He then said: "Whenever a closed case is sent up to the Secretariat, if there is doubt about severity, it is always sent back for reconsideration. Since the power is unequal, judicial officials shrink back and delay.

sentences.zh: 請自今以疑獄讞者，皆得輕論。」

translations.literal: I request that from now on, in cases where the sentence is doubtful, lighter judgments may all be given."
translations.idiomatic: I request that from now on, in cases where the sentence is doubtful, lighter judgments may be given."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 求知陳州，還，為龍圖閣直學士、判軍器監。

translations.literal: He requested appointment as Prefect of Chenzhou. On his return he became Direct Academic of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Judge of the Directorate of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: He requested appointment as prefect of Chenzhou. On his return he became direct academic of the Dragon Diagram Hall and judge of the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 命館遼使。

translations.literal: He was ordered to host the Liao envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to host the Liao envoys.

sentences.zh: 方宴近郊，使者不令其徒分坐廡下，力爭之，使無以奪。

translations.literal: When they were feasting in the suburbs, the envoys would not allow their attendants to sit separately in the side halls. Dao argued forcefully, and the envoys had no way to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When they were feasting in the suburbs, the envoys would not allow their attendants to sit separately in the side halls. Dao argued forcefully, and the envoys could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 至肄儀將見，又不使綴行分班，使者入，餘皆坐門外，燾請令門見而出，眾始愧悔。

translations.literal: When it came to rehearsing the rites before the audience, they again would not allow the attendants to follow in procession according to rank. The envoys entered while the rest all sat outside the gate. Dao requested that they be allowed to enter at the gate and leave at the gate; only then did the group begin to feel shame and regret.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to rehearsing the rites before the audience, they again would not allow the attendants to follow in procession according to rank. The envoys entered while the rest all sat outside the gate. Dao requested that they be allowed to enter and leave through the gate; only then did the group begin to feel shame and regret.

sentences.zh: 逮辭日，悉如儀。

translations.literal: By the day of farewell, everything was according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: By the day of farewell, everything was conducted according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 或謂細故無足較，燾曰：「契丹喜嘗試人，其漸不可長也。」

translations.literal: Some said these were minor matters not worth disputing. Dao said: "The Khitan like to test people; such encroachments cannot be allowed to grow."
translations.idiomatic: Some said these were minor matters not worth disputing. Dao said: "The Khitan like to test people; such encroachments cannot be allowed to grow."

sentences.zh: 俄權三司使，改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made Acting Commissioner of the Three Departments and changed to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made acting commissioner of the Three Departments and then minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 六年。

translations.literal: In the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 同知樞密院。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏人款塞，乞還侵疆。

translations.literal: The Xia people came to the border with expressions of goodwill and asked to have the invaded territory returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Xia came to the border with expressions of goodwill and asked to have the invaded territory returned.

sentences.zh: 燾言：「地有非要害者固宜予，然羌情無厭，當使知吾宥過而息兵，不應示以厭兵之意。」

translations.literal: Dao said: "Land that is not strategically vital may indeed be granted, yet the Qiang temperament knows no satiety. We should let them know that we pardon their faults and cease hostilities—we should not show them that we are weary of war."
translations.idiomatic: Dao said: "Land that is not strategically vital may indeed be granted, yet the Qiang temperament knows no satiety. We should let them know that we pardon their faults and cease hostilities—we should not show them that we are weary of war."

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，復仍前議，二府遂欲並棄熙河。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, the earlier proposal was revived, and the two councils then wished to abandon Hexi entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, the earlier proposal was revived, and the two councils then wished to abandon Hexi entirely.

sentences.zh: 燾固爭之，曰：「自靈武而東，皆中國故地。

translations.literal: Dao firmly opposed this, saying: "From Lingwu eastward, all is former territory of China.
translations.idiomatic: Dao firmly opposed this, saying: "From Lingwu eastward, all is former territory of China.

sentences.zh: 先帝有此武功，今無故棄之，豈不取輕於外夷？」

translations.literal: The late emperor achieved this military merit; if we now abandon it for no reason, will we not be held in contempt by the outer barbarians?"
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor achieved this military merit. If we now abandon it for no reason, will we not be held in contempt by foreign peoples?"

sentences.zh: 於是但以葭蘆等四砦歸之。

translations.literal: Thereupon only the four forts of Jialu and the like were returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end only the four forts at Jialu and the like were returned to them.

sentences.zh: 蔡確輩更用事，燾循循其間，不能有所建明。

translations.literal: Cai Que and his faction came to power again; Dao moved deferentially among them and could accomplish nothing notable.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que and his faction came to power again. Dao moved deferentially among them and could accomplish nothing of note.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，進知院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou, he was promoted to director of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanyou (1087), he was promoted to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時復洮、河，擒鬼章青宜結，二邊少清，而幷塞猶苦寇掠。

translations.literal: At that time Tao and He were recovered, Gui Zhang Qingyijie was captured, the two frontiers were somewhat quiet, yet the border garrisons still suffered from raids.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tao and He were recovered and Gui Zhang Qingyijie was captured; the two frontiers grew somewhat quiet, yet the border garrisons still suffered from enemy raids.

sentences.zh: 燾言：「為國者不可好用兵，亦不可畏用兵，好則疲民，畏則遺患。

translations.literal: Dao said: "One who governs a state must neither be fond of using troops nor fear using troops; fondness exhausts the people, fear leaves behind calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Dao said: "A ruler must neither be fond of war nor afraid of war. Fondness exhausts the people; fear leaves trouble behind.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷每戒疆吏，非舉國入寇毋得應之，則固畏用兵矣。

translations.literal: Now the court constantly admonishes frontier officials that unless the enemy invades with the whole nation they must not respond—this is indeed fearing the use of troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court now constantly warns frontier officials that they must not respond unless the enemy invades in full force—this is plainly fear of war.

sentences.zh: 雖僅保障戍，實墮其計中，願復講攻擾之策。

translations.literal: Although we only barely protect the garrisons, in fact we fall into their stratagem; I wish we would again discuss policies of attack and harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Though we barely hold the garrisons secure, we have in fact fallen into their trap. I ask that we resume policies of attack and harassment.

sentences.zh: 且乾順幼豎，梁氏擅權，族黨酋渠多反側顧望。

translations.literal: Moreover Qianshun is young, the Liang clan monopolizes power, and many tribal chiefs and clan leaders are wavering and looking about.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Qianshun is still a boy, the Liang clan holds power, and many chiefs and clan leaders are wavering and watching which way to turn.

sentences.zh: 若有以離間之，未必不回戈而復怨，此一奇也。」

translations.literal: If someone were to sow discord among them, they might well turn their blades back and renew their resentments—this would be one extraordinary stroke."
translations.idiomatic: If we could sow discord among them, they might well turn their blades on one another and renew old grievances—that would be a singular opportunity."

sentences.zh: 其後夏人自相攜貳，使來修貢，悉如燾策。

translations.literal: Afterward the Xia people turned against one another, sent envoys to pay tribute—all exactly as Dao had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Western Xia split among themselves and sent envoys to pay tribute—everything unfolded as Dao had urged.

sentences.zh: 宣仁太后患國用不足，頗裁冗費，宗室奉亦在議中。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren was troubled that state revenue was insufficient and considerably cut redundant expenses; imperial clan stipends were also under discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren worried that state revenue was insufficient and cut many redundant expenses; even stipends for the imperial clan came under discussion.

sentences.zh: 燾諫曰：「陛下雖痛抑外家，以示至公，然此舉不可不深思而熟計。」

translations.literal: Dao remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty, though you sternly restrain your mother's kin to show utmost fairness, this measure cannot fail to be deeply considered and carefully planned."
translations.idiomatic: Dao remonstrated: "Your Majesty may wish to restrain your mother's kin severely to show utmost fairness, yet this step must be weighed with deep thought and careful planning."

sentences.zh: 太后悟，遂止。

translations.literal: The empress dowager understood and thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager took his point and dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 大河北流，宰相主水官議，必欲回之東注。

translations.literal: The Yellow River flowed north; the chief councillors upheld the water officials' proposal and were determined to turn it back to flow east.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River was flowing north. The chief councillors backed the water officials and insisted on diverting it eastward again.

sentences.zh: 燾以河流入濼淀，久必淤淺，恐河朔無以禦敵，遂上言曰：「自小吳未決之前，河雖屢徙，而盡在中國，故京師得以為北限。

translations.literal: Dao argued that with the river entering the marshlands of Liaodian, over time it would certainly silt up and become shallow, and he feared that Hebei would have no means to resist the enemy; he therefore submitted a memorial saying: "Before the breach at Xiaowu, though the river shifted many times, it all remained within China, so the capital could take it as the northern boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Dao held that once the river entered the Liaodian marshes it would inevitably silt up and grow shallow, leaving Hebei unable to resist the enemy. He memorialized the throne: "Before the breach at Xiaowu, though the river shifted often, it always stayed within our realm, so the capital could rely on it as the northern barrier.

sentences.zh: 今決而西，則河尾益北，如此不已，將南岸遂屬敵界。

translations.literal: Now that it has burst and flowed west, the river's terminus grows ever more northerly; if this continues without end, the south bank will in time belong to enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Now that it has broken westward, the river's lower course drifts ever north. If this goes on, the south bank will eventually lie in enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 彼若建橋梁，守以州郡，窺兵河外，可為寒心。

translations.literal: If they build bridges and garrison it with prefectures and districts, watching for troops beyond the river—it is cause for dread.
translations.idiomatic: If they build bridges and hold the line with prefectures and districts, they can probe for troops beyond the river—a chilling prospect.

sentences.zh: 今水官之議，不過論地形，較功費；

translations.literal: The water officials' proposal today goes no further than discussing terrain and comparing labor and expense;
translations.idiomatic: The water officials' plan today goes no further than terrain and cost;

sentences.zh: 而獻納之臣，不考利害輕重，徒便於治河，而以設險為緩，非至計也。」

translations.literal: yet the ministers who present counsel do not weigh advantage and harm, light and heavy; they only find it convenient to regulate the river and treat establishing defenses as something to defer—not the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: yet the remonstrating ministers never weigh benefit against harm. They only want what is convenient for managing the river and treat fortifying the frontier as something to put off—not the best policy."

sentences.zh: 帝雖然之，而回河之議紛起，東北蕭然煩費，功亦不就。

translations.literal: The emperor assented in principle, but proposals to turn the river back arose in confusion; the northeast was bleak with expense, and the work also failed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed in principle, but debate over diverting the river raged on. The northeast was drained by expense, and the project never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 三年，同列皆序遷，且新用執政，燾獨如初。

translations.literal: In the third year, all his peers were promoted in orderly succession, and new men held chief power—Dao alone remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year all his colleagues were promoted in turn while new men took power at the top; Dao alone stayed where he was.

sentences.zh: 詔增其兩秩，燾懇辭曰：「是雖有故事，竊意以一時同列超升之故，特用是以慰安其心爾。

translations.literal: An edict increased him by two ranks; Dao earnestly declined, saying: "Though there is precedent for this, I privately think that because at one stroke all peers were promoted above him, this was specially used to comfort his heart.
translations.idiomatic: An edict raised him two ranks. Dao earnestly declined: "There is precedent, but I suspect that because everyone else was promoted at once, this was meant only to soothe one man's feelings.

sentences.zh: 今日願自臣革之，使朝廷不為姑息，而大臣稍敦廉恥之風，庶或有補。」

translations.literal: Today I wish to abolish it myself from my person, so that the court does not indulge in favoritism and great ministers somewhat cultivate the wind of integrity and shame—perhaps there may be some benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Today I ask to give it up myself, so the court does not indulge favoritism and senior ministers may recover a little of their sense of honor—perhaps that will help."

sentences.zh: 竟不受。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He never accepted the promotion.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去，卒喪，拜觀文殿學士、知鄭州，徙潁昌及河南府，入為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his mother's mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and prefect of Zhengzhou, transferred to Yingchang and Henan prefectures, and entered the capital as vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother. When mourning ended he was made academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and prefect of Zhengzhou, then moved to Yingchang and Henan, and finally entered the capital as vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣仁之喪，宗室既為三年服，才越歲，章惇拜相，欲革為期。

translations.literal: For the mourning of Xuanren, the imperial clan had already worn three-year mourning; barely a year had passed when Zhang Dun became chief councillor and wished to change it to one year.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanren's death the imperial clan had already been in three-year mourning. Barely a year later Zhang Dun became chief councillor and wanted to shorten it to one year.

sentences.zh: 燾爭之曰：「上以先后保佑之久，追崇如恐不盡，茲用明道故實耳。

translations.literal: Dao disputed this, saying: "The emperor, because the late empresses long protected the realm, honors them as if he feared he could not do enough—hence he uses the precedents of the Mingdao era.
translations.idiomatic: Dao objected: "The emperor, because the late empresses long watched over the realm, honors them as though he can never do enough—that is why he follows the Mingdao precedents.

sentences.zh: 遽改之，播諸天下，非佳聲也。」

translations.literal: To change this hastily and broadcast it throughout the realm is not a fine reputation."
translations.idiomatic: To change that hastily and proclaim it to the empire would not sound well."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The change was dropped.

sentences.zh: 燾與惇布衣交，覬其助己，燾不肯少下之。

translations.literal: Dao and Dun had been friends as commoners; Dun hoped he would help him, but Dao would not yield to him in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Dao and Dun had been friends in plain clothes. Dun expected his help, but Dao would not defer to him in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 陽翟民蓋漸有財訟，而與諫官來之邵交通，開封得其事。

translations.literal: A man of Yangdi named Gai Jian had a property dispute and was in contact with the remonstrator Lai Zhi Shao; Kaifeng uncovered the affair.
translations.idiomatic: A Yangdi man named Gai Jian was embroiled in a property lawsuit and was in contact with the remonstrator Lai Zhi Shao; Kaifeng uncovered the case.

sentences.zh: 惇右之邵，欲薄其罪，燾不可；

translations.literal: Dun favored Shao and wished to lighten his offense; Dao would not agree;
translations.idiomatic: Dun sided with Shao and wanted to lighten his sentence; Dao refused;

sentences.zh: 復欲並劾開封，燾又不可，遂與惇隙。

translations.literal: he then wished to impeach Kaifeng as well, and Dao again refused—thereupon he and Dun fell out.
translations.idiomatic: Dun then wanted to impeach Kaifeng as well, and Dao refused again. He and Dun broke with each other.

sentences.zh: 明堂齋祠，為儀仗使，後官有絕馳道穿仗而過者，燾方舉劾，諫官常安民又言，教坊不當於相國寺作樂。

translations.literal: At the Bright Hall fasting sacrifice, Dao served as master of ceremonies; a rear palace woman crossed the imperial roadway through the guard of honor, and Dao was just about to impeach her when the remonstrator Chang Anmin also spoke, saying the Music Bureau should not perform at Xiangguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the Bright Hall fasting rites Dao was master of ceremonies. A palace woman cut across the imperial roadway through the guard of honor; Dao was about to impeach her when the remonstrator Chang Anmin also spoke, saying the Music Bureau should not perform at Xiangguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲逐安民，燾為救釋。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to expel Anmin; Dao secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and wanted to drive Anmin out; Dao pleaded and secured his pardon.

sentences.zh: 惇遂譖其相表裏，出知鄭州，徙大名。

translations.literal: Dun then slandered them as acting in concert and had Dao sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou, then transferred to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Dun then accused them of acting in concert and had Dao sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou, then moved him to Daming.

sentences.zh: 父日華，本三班院吏，以燾恩封光祿大夫，至是卒，年九十餘，燾免喪。

translations.literal: His father Rihua had originally been a clerk in the Third Class Bureau; through Dao's favor he was enfeoffed as Grandee of Splendid Happiness; at this time he died, aged more than ninety; Dao ended his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rihua had been a clerk in the Third Class Bureau and, through Dao's influence, was enfeoffed as Grandee of Splendid Happiness. He now died at more than ninety, and Dao left mourning.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復知樞密院。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, Dao again became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, Dao again became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 舊制，內侍出使，以所得旨言於院，審實乃得行。

translations.literal: Under the old system, when inner attendants went on missions they reported the orders they had received to the bureau, and only after verification could they proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, when eunuchs went on missions they had to report the orders they carried to the bureau; only after verification could they act.

sentences.zh: 後多輒去，燾請按治之。

translations.literal: Later many simply left without doing so; Dao requested that they be investigated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Later many simply left without reporting. Dao asked that they be investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 都知閻守懃領他職，祈罷不以告，亦劾之，帝敕守懃詣燾謝。

translations.literal: The director Yan Shouqin held another post and requested to resign without informing him; Dao impeached him as well, and the emperor ordered Shouqin to go to Dao and apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The director Yan Shouqin took another post and asked to resign without telling him; Dao impeached him too, and the emperor ordered Shouqin to apologize to Dao in person.

sentences.zh: 郝隨得罪，或揣上意且起用，欲援赦為階，亦爭之。

translations.literal: Hao Sui had been punished; some guessed the emperor might soon recall him and wished to use an amnesty as the step; Dao disputed this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Sui had been punished. Some guessed the emperor might soon recall him and tried to use an amnesty as the opening; Dao objected again.

sentences.zh: 以老避位，帝將寵以觀文殿大學士，有間之者曰：「是宰相恩典也。」

translations.literal: Because of age he sought to leave office; the emperor was about to honor him with the grand academician title of the Hall for Observing Culture, but someone intervened, saying: "That is a chief councillor's grace."
translations.idiomatic: He sought to retire on account of age. The emperor was about to honor him as grand academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, but someone whispered: "That is a chief councillor's privilege."

sentences.zh: 但以學士知河南。

translations.literal: He was made only academician and prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given only the lower academician title and made prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 將行，上疏曰：「自紹聖、元符以來，用事之臣，持紹述之名，誑惑君父，上則固寵位而快恩仇，下則希進用而肆朋附。

translations.literal: Before departing he submitted a memorial, saying: "Since the Shaosheng and Yuanfu eras, the ministers in power, wielding the name of continuing the late emperor's policies, deceived ruler and father; above they secured favor and gratified private enmities, below they hoped for advancement and indulged in faction.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left he submitted a memorial: "Since the Shaosheng and Yuanfu reigns, men in power, waving the banner of continuing the late emperor's work, have misled ruler and father. Above they cling to favor and settle scores; below they crave promotion and run in packs.

sentences.zh: 彼自為謀則善矣，未嚐有毫髮為公家計者也。

translations.literal: For their own schemes they did well enough, yet never once spared a hair's breadth of thought for the public good.
translations.idiomatic: They have schemed well for themselves, but never once spared a thought for the state.

sentences.zh: 夫聽言之道，必以其事觀之。

translations.literal: The way to hear words is to judge them by their deeds.
translations.idiomatic: The way to judge speech is to look at what it produces.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢高談遠引，獨以神考之事切於今者為證。

translations.literal: Your servant dares not discourse loftily from distant examples; I take only matters of the late Shenzong that bear on today as proof.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not reach for lofty examples from afar. I will use only what touches us today from the late Shenzong's reign as proof.

sentences.zh: 熙寧、元豐之間，中外府庫，無不充衍，小邑所積錢米，亦不減二十萬，紹聖以還，傾竭以供邊費，使軍無見糧，吏無月俸，公私虛耗，未有甚於此時，而反謂紹述，豈不為厚誣哉！

translations.literal: Between the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, treasuries at court and in the provinces were all full; even small districts stored no less than two hundred thousand in cash and grain. Since Shaosheng, everything has been drained to supply frontier expenses, so that armies have no grain in sight and officials no monthly salary; public and private stores have been emptied as never in this period—yet they still call it continuing the late emperor's policies. Is this not a gross deception!
translations.idiomatic: Under Xining and Yuanfeng, treasuries at court and in the provinces overflowed; even small districts held no less than two hundred thousand in cash and grain. Since Shaosheng everything has been poured into the frontier, until armies see no grain and officials receive no monthly pay. Public and private stores have never been so empty—yet they still call it "continuing the late emperor's work." What gross deception is this!

sentences.zh: 願陛下監之，勿使飾偏辭而為身謀者復得行其說。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to watch for this and not let those who dress up partial words for private ends again have their say."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to watch for this and not let men who polish one-sided arguments for private gain speak again."

sentences.zh: 又言：「東京黨禍已萌，願戒履霜之漸。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The party strife of the eastern capital has already sprouted; I wish you to guard against the frost that foretells ice."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Factional strife in the eastern capital has already begun. I beg you to heed the frost that warns of ice ahead."

sentences.zh: 語尤激切。

translations.literal: His words were especially forceful.
translations.idiomatic: His language was especially sharp.

sentences.zh: 初，建青唐邈川為湟州，戍守困於供億。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qingtang Moyuchuan had been made into Huang prefecture, and the garrison was distressed by supply costs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qingtang Moyuchuan had been made Huang prefecture, and the garrison was crushed by the cost of supplies.

sentences.zh: 燾在樞府，因議者以為可棄，奏還之。

translations.literal: While Dao was at the Bureau of Military Affairs, because debaters thought it could be abandoned, he memorialized to return it.
translations.idiomatic: While Dao was at the bureau, debaters argued it could be abandoned, and he memorialized to give it up.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年議其罪，降端明殿學士，再貶寧國軍節度副使，漢陽軍安置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning his offense was debated; he was demoted to academician of the Bright Hall, then again demoted to vice military commissioner of Ningguo army and settled at Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning (1102) his offense was debated. He was demoted to academician of the Bright Hall, then again to vice military commissioner of Ningguo and settled at Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 湟州復，又降祁州團練副使。

translations.literal: When Huang prefecture was recovered, he was demoted again to vice training commissioner of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang was recovered he was demoted again to vice training commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 鄯州之復，又移建昌軍，然棄鄯州時，燾居憂不預也，終不敢自明。

translations.literal: When Shan prefecture was recovered, he was moved to Jianchang; yet when Shan was abandoned, Dao was in mourning and did not take part—yet in the end he never dared clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Shan was recovered he was moved to Jianchang. Yet when Shan was abandoned Dao was in mourning and had no part in the decision; still he never dared clear his name.

sentences.zh: 閱再歲，始復通議大夫，還洛卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: After nearly two years he was restored to Grandee for Discussion, returned to Luoyang, and died there at seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: After nearly two years he was restored to Grandee for Discussion, returned to Luoyang, and died there at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 後五歲，悉還其官職。

translations.literal: Five years later all his offices were fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later all his offices were fully restored.

sentences.zh: 子扶，靖康時為給事中。

translations.literal: His son Fu, at the time of Jingkang, was a supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu was a supervising secretary at the time of the Jingkang crisis.

sentences.zh: 金人入京師，責取金帛，扶與梅執禮、陳知質、程振皆見殺。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens entered the capital and demanded gold and silk, Fu together with Mei Zhili, Chen Zhizhi, and Cheng Zhen were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens entered the capital and demanded gold and silk, Fu was killed together with Mei Zhili, Chen Zhizhi, and Cheng Zhen.

sentences.zh: 張璪，初名琥，字邃明，滁州全椒人，洎之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zao, originally named Hu, styled Suiming, was a man of Quanjiao in Chuzhou, grandson of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zao, originally named Hu, styled Suiming, was from Quanjiao in Chuzhou and was the grandson of Zhang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 早孤，鞠於兄環，欲任以官，辭不就。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he was raised by his elder brother Huan, who wished to give him an office; he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his elder brother Huan, who wanted to give him an official post; he refused.

sentences.zh: 未冠登第，歷鳳翔法曹、縉雲令。

translations.literal: Before coming of age he passed the examinations and served as legal officer at Fengxiang and magistrate of Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he passed the examinations and served as legal officer at Fengxiang and magistrate of Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 王安石與環善，既得政，將用之，而環已老，乃引璪同編修中書條例，授集賢校理、知諫院、直舍人院。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi was friendly with Huan; once he gained power he was about to employ him, but Huan was already old, so he brought in Zao to compile together the regulations of the Central Secretariat, appointing him collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, remonstrator, and direct attendant of the Academy Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was friendly with Huan. Once in power he meant to employ Huan, but Huan was already old, so he brought in Zao to help compile the Secretariat regulations and appointed him collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, remonstrator, and direct attendant of the Academy Palace.

sentences.zh: 楊繪、劉摯論助役，安石使璪為文詰之，辭，曾布請為之，由是忤安石意。

translations.literal: Yang Hui and Liu Zhi debated the labor-exemption levy; Anshi had Zao write a piece to refute them; he declined; Zeng Bu asked to do it, and thereby offended Anshi's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hui and Liu Zhi attacked the labor-exemption levy. Anshi had Zao write a rebuttal; Zao refused. Zeng Bu volunteered and thereby fell out of Anshi's favor.

sentences.zh: 神宗欲命璪知制誥，安石薦用布，以璪同修起居注。

translations.literal: Shenzong wished to appoint Zao drafter of edicts; Anshi recommended Bu instead and made Zao co-compiler of the diary.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong wanted to make Zao drafter of edicts. Anshi recommended Bu instead and made Zao co-compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 自縣令至是，才歲餘。

translations.literal: From magistrate to this post was barely more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: From county magistrate to this post took barely a year.

sentences.zh: 坐奏事不實，解三職，已而復之。

translations.literal: He was punished for reporting matters untruthfully, stripped of three posts, then soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for reporting untruthfully, stripped of three posts, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 時建議武學，璪言：「古之太學，舞干習射，受成獻功，莫不在焉。

translations.literal: At that time a military academy was proposed; Zao said: "In antiquity the Imperial Academy practiced shield dances and archery, received completed work and presented achievements—all were there.
translations.idiomatic: When a military academy was proposed, Zao said: "The ancient Imperial Academy taught shield dances and archery, received completed work and presented achievements—all of it was there.

sentences.zh: 文武之才，皆自此出，未聞偏習其一者也。

translations.literal: Talents civil and military all came from this; one never heard of training only one side.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military talent alike came from it. No one ever heard of training only one side.

sentences.zh: 請無問文武之士，一養於太學。」

translations.literal: I ask that civil and military scholars alike be nurtured in one Imperial Academy."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that civil and military students alike be trained in the single Imperial Academy."

sentences.zh: 朝廷既復河、隴，欲因勢戡定夔、蜀、荊、廣諸夷，璪言：「先王務治中國而已。

translations.literal: The court had already recovered He and Long and wished to take advantage and pacify the Yi of Kui, Shu, Jing, and Guang; Zao said: "The former kings devoted themselves to governing China alone.
translations.idiomatic: The court had recovered He and Long and wished to press on and subdue the Yi of Kui, Shu, Jing, and Guang. Zao said: "The former kings devoted themselves to governing China alone.

sentences.zh: 今生財未盡有道，用財未盡有禮，不宜遽及徂征之事。」

translations.literal: Today revenue is not yet fully governed by the Way, expenditure is not yet fully governed by ritual—it is not fitting hastily to undertake distant campaigns."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue is not yet fully ordered by the Way, expenditure not yet fully ordered by ritual. It is not yet time to rush into distant campaigns."

sentences.zh: 皆不聽。

translations.literal: None of this was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: None of it was heeded.

sentences.zh: 以集賢殿修撰知蔡州，復知諫院兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: As academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he became prefect of Cai; he again became remonstrator and concurrently supervising censor with chief responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: As academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he became prefect of Cai, then again remonstrator and concurrently supervising censor with chief responsibility.

sentences.zh: 盧秉行鹽法於東南，操持峻急，一人抵禁，數家為黥徙，且破產以償告捕，二年中犯者萬人。

translations.literal: Lu Bing carried out the salt law in the southeast with harsh severity; one person violated the ban and several households were tattooed and exiled, and their property was ruined to pay informers; in two years ten thousand offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bing enforced the salt monopoly in the southeast with harsh severity. One violation could bring tattooing and exile for several households and ruin their property to pay informers. In two years there were ten thousand offenders.

sentences.zh: 璪條列其狀。

translations.literal: Zao itemized the situation in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zao laid out the facts in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 又言：「行役法以來，最下戶亦每歲納錢，乞度寬羨數均損之，以惠貧弱。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Since the labor-service law, even the poorest households pay money each year; I ask that surplus funds be calculated and averaged to reduce the burden, to benefit the poor and weak."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Since the labor-service law even the poorest households pay cash every year. I ask that surplus funds be calculated and shared to lighten the burden on the poor."

sentences.zh: 後皆施行。

translations.literal: Later all were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Later all were carried out.

sentences.zh: 鄭俠事起，璪媚呂惠卿，劾馮京與俠交通有跡，深其辭，致京等於罪。

translations.literal: When the Zheng Xia affair arose, Zao curried favor with Lu Huiqing and impeached Feng Jing for having traces of contact with Xia, deepening the charges and bringing Jing and others to conviction.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zheng Xia affair broke out, Zao curried favor with Lu Huiqing and impeached Feng Jing for traces of contact with Xia, deepening the charges until Jing and others were convicted.

sentences.zh: 判司農寺，出知河陽。

translations.literal: He was made director of the Directorate of Agriculture and sent out as prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Directorate of Agriculture and sent out as prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，入權度支副使，遂知制誥、知諫院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng he entered as acting vice director of revenue, then became drafter of edicts and remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanfeng he entered as acting vice director of revenue, then became drafter of edicts and remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 判國子監，薦蔡卞可為直講。

translations.literal: As director of the Directorate of Education he recommended Cai Bian as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: As director of the Directorate of Education he recommended Cai Bian as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 建增博士弟子員，月書、季考，歲校，以行藝次升，略仿《周官》鄉比之法，立齋舍八十二。

translations.literal: He proposed increasing the number of doctoral disciples, monthly writing, quarterly examinations, and annual review, promoting by order of conduct and achievement, roughly following the village comparison method of the "Rites of Zhou," and established eighty-two dormitories.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed increasing doctoral students, monthly essays, quarterly exams, and annual review, promoting by conduct and achievement in rough imitation of the village comparison method in the "Rites of Zhou," and established eighty-two dormitories.

sentences.zh: 學官之盛，近代莫比，其議多自璪發之。

translations.literal: The flourishing of the schools in recent times had no parallel; most of the proposals came from Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Schools had never flourished so in recent times; most of the plan came from Zao.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾下臺獄，璪與李定雜治，謀傅致軾於死，卒不克。

translations.literal: When Su Shi was sent to the censorial prison, Zao together with Li Ding jointly prosecuted him, plotting to frame Shi with a capital charge, but in the end they did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was sent to the censorial prison, Zao and Li Ding jointly prosecuted him, plotting to frame him on a capital charge, but failed.

sentences.zh: 詳定郊廟奉祀禮文，議者多以國朝未嘗躬行方澤之禮為非，正詔議更制。

translations.literal: He detailed the ritual texts for suburban and temple sacrifices; debaters mostly held it wrong that the dynasty had never personally performed the square-marsh rite, and an edict ordered discussion of reform.
translations.idiomatic: He worked on ritual texts for suburban and temple sacrifices. Critics mostly held it wrong that the dynasty had never personally performed the square-marsh rite, and an edict ordered reform.

sentences.zh: 璪請於夏至之日，備禮容樂舞，以塚宰攝事。

translations.literal: Zao asked that on the summer solstice full ritual, music, and dance be prepared, with the chief minister presiding.
translations.idiomatic: Zao asked that on the summer solstice full ritual, music, and dance be prepared, with the chief minister presiding.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「在今所宜，無以易此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For what is fitting today, nothing should replace this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "For what is fitting today, nothing should replace this."

sentences.zh: 卒行其說。

translations.literal: In the end his proposal was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his proposal was carried out.

sentences.zh: 為翰林學士，詳定官制，以寄祿二十四階易前日省、寺虛名，而職事名始正。

translations.literal: As academician of the Hanlin he detailed the official system, replacing the former empty titles of the ministries and directorates with twenty-four salary ranks for stipendiary posts, so that the names of actual duties were at last correct.
translations.idiomatic: As Hanlin academician he worked on the official system, replacing the old empty titles of ministries and directorates with twenty-four stipendiary ranks so that actual duties at last had correct names.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜參知政事，改中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made vice grand councillor and changed to vice director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made vice grand councillor and changed to vice director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，諫官、御史合攻之，謂：「璪奸邪便佞，善窺主意，隨勢所在而依附之，往往以危機陷人。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended the throne, remonstrators and censors jointly attacked him, saying: "Zao is treacherous and fawning, skilled at probing the ruler's intent and attaching himself wherever power lies, often trapping people with deadly charges.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong took the throne, remonstrators and censors attacked him together, saying: "Zao is treacherous and fawning, skilled at reading the ruler's mind and clinging wherever power sits, often trapping people with deadly charges.

sentences.zh: 深交舒亶，數起大獄，天下共知其為大奸。

translations.literal: He was deeply connected with Shu Dan and repeatedly launched great prosecutions; all under heaven knew him as a great villain.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Shu Dan and repeatedly launched major prosecutions. Everyone knew him as a great villain.

sentences.zh: 小人而在高位，德之賊也。」

translations.literal: A petty man in a high place is the enemy of virtue."
translations.idiomatic: A petty man in high office is virtue's enemy."

sentences.zh: 疏入，皆不報。

translations.literal: The memorials entered but none were answered.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials went in but none were answered.

sentences.zh: 最後，劉摯言：「璪初奉安石，旋附惠卿，隨王珪，黨章惇，諂蔡確，數人之性不同，而能探情變節，左右從順，各得其歡心。

translations.literal: Finally Liu Zhi said: "Zao at first served Anshi, then attached to Huiqing, followed Wang Gui, joined Zhang Dun's faction, and flattered Cai Que—these men differ in nature, yet he could probe their feelings, change his manner, and follow left and right, winning each man's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Finally Liu Zhi said: "Zao first served Anshi, then Huiqing, then Wang Gui, then Zhang Dun's faction, then Cai Que. These men differ in character, yet he could read their moods, shift his manner, and follow each in turn, winning every man's favor.

sentences.zh: 今過惡既章，不可不速去。」

translations.literal: Now his offenses are clear; he must be removed swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: Now his crimes are plain. He must be removed at once."

sentences.zh: 如是逾歲，乃以資政殿學士知鄭州，徙河南、定州、大名府，進大學士，知揚州以卒。

translations.literal: Thus for more than a year; then he was made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Zhengzhou, transferred to Henan, Ding, and Daming prefectures, advanced to grand academician, and died as prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year passed in this way before he was made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Zhengzhou, then moved to Henan, Ding, and Daming, advanced to grand academician, and died as prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 贈右銀青光祿大夫，諡曰「簡翼」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Right Silver-Glitter Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with the posthumous name "Simple and Aiding."
