translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title Right Silver-Glitter Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with posthumous name Jianyi ("Simple and Aiding").

sentences.zh: 蒲宗孟

translations.literal: Pu Zongmeng
translations.idiomatic: Pu Zongmeng

sentences.zh: 蒲宗孟，字傳正，閬州新井人。

translations.literal: Pu Zongmeng, styled Chuanzheng, was a man of Xinjin in Lang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Zongmeng, styled Chuanzheng, was from Xinjin in Lang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調夔州觀察推官。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations for presented scholar and was appointed investigating officer of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating officer of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 治平中，水災地震，宗孟上書，斥大臣及宮禁、宦寺，熙寧元年，改著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era, when flood and earthquake struck, Zongmeng submitted a memorial denouncing great ministers and the palace, eunuchs, and inner attendants. In the first year of Xining he was made assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era, when floods and earthquakes struck, Zongmeng submitted a memorial attacking great ministers and the palace eunuchs. In the first year of Xining (1068) he was made assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 神宗見其名，曰：「是嘗言水災地震者邪？」

translations.literal: Shenzong saw his name and said: "Is this the one who spoke of flood and earthquake?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong saw his name and said: "Is this the man who spoke about the floods and earthquakes?"

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，以為館閣校勘、檢正中書戶房兼修條例，進集賢校理。

translations.literal: He was summoned to test at the Academy, made collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, rectifier of the Central Secretariat household registry while compiling regulations, and advanced to collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to test at the Hanlin Academy, appointed collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and rectifier of the Central Secretariat household registry while compiling regulations, then promoted to collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 時三司新置提舉帳司官，祿豐地要，人人欲得之。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Departments newly established the post of commissioner for ledger accounts, with rich salary and important station; everyone wished to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments had just created the post of commissioner for ledger accounts, with a rich salary and important station, and everyone wanted it.

sentences.zh: 執政上其員，帝命與宗孟。

translations.literal: The chief councillors presented their candidates; the emperor ordered it given to Zongmeng.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillors presented their candidates; the emperor gave the post to Zongmeng.

sentences.zh: 命察訪荊湖兩路，奏罷辰、沅役錢及湖南丁賦，遠人賴之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to inspect the Jing and Hu circuits, memorialized to abolish corvee money in Chen and Yuan and the ding tax in Hunan; distant people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to inspect Jing and Hu, he memorialized to abolish corvee levies in Chen and Yuan and the ding tax in Hunan, to the great relief of people in distant districts.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿制手實法，然猶許災傷五分以上不預。

translations.literal: Lu Huiqing devised the household inventory law, yet still allowed those with disaster losses of five-tenths or more not to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huiqing devised the household inventory law but still exempted households with disaster losses of fifty percent or more.

sentences.zh: 宗孟言：「民以手實上其家之物產而官為注籍，以正百年無用不明之版圖而均齊其力役，天下良法也。

translations.literal: Zongmeng said: "The people report their household property by hand for official registration, to correct century-old useless and unclear land registers and equalize labor duties—this is a fine law for all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmeng said: "Having households report their property for official registration corrects century-old useless land registers and equalizes labor duties—a fine law for the realm.

sentences.zh: 然災傷五分不預焉。

translations.literal: Yet disaster losses of five-tenths are not included.
translations.idiomatic: Yet households with disaster losses of fifty percent are excluded.

sentences.zh: 臣以為使民自供，初無所擾，何待豐歲？

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that having the people supply information themselves disturbs nothing at first—why wait for a bountiful year?
translations.idiomatic: I believe self-reporting disturbs nothing at the outset—why wait for a good harvest year?

sentences.zh: 願詔有司，勿以豐凶弛張其法。」

translations.literal: I wish an edict to the responsible offices not to tighten or loosen the law according to good or bad harvests."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that responsible offices be ordered not to tighten or loosen the law according to harvests."

sentences.zh: 從之，民於是益病矣。

translations.literal: This was followed, and the people were thus further afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, and the people were further afflicted.

sentences.zh: 俄同修起居注、直舍人院、知制誥，帝又稱其有史才，命同修兩朝國史，為翰林學士兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon he was co-compiler of the diary, direct attendant of the Academy Palace, and drafter of edicts. The emperor also praised his talent for history and ordered him to co-compile the national history of two reigns, making him Hanlin academician and attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was co-compiler of the imperial diary, direct attendant of the Academy Palace, and drafter of edicts. The emperor also praised his historical talent and had him co-compile the national history of two reigns, appointing him Hanlin academician and attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 舊制，學士唯服金帶，宗孟入謝，帝曰：「學士職清地近，非他官比，而官儀未寵。」

translations.literal: Under the old system academics wore only the gold belt. When Zongmeng came to give thanks, the emperor said: "The academician's post is pure and close to the throne, not comparable to other offices, yet the official insignia is not honored enough."
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules Hanlin academics wore only the gold belt. When Zongmeng came to give thanks, the emperor said: "The Hanlin post is pure and close to the throne, unlike other offices, yet its insignia are not honored enough."

sentences.zh: 乃加佩魚，遂著為令。

translations.literal: He was therefore given the fish tally as well, and this was established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the fish tally as well, and this became a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 樞密都承旨張誠一預書局事，頗肆橫，挾中旨以脅同列。

translations.literal: Zhang Chengyi, chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, took part in the bureau for compiling the history and was quite overbearing, using secret imperial orders to intimidate his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengyi, chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, took part in compiling the history and was overbearing, using secret imperial orders to intimidate colleagues.

sentences.zh: 宗孟持其語質帝前，皆非是，因叩頭白其奸。

translations.literal: Zongmeng took his words before the emperor to verify them; none were correct, and he kowtowed to report his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmeng brought his statements before the emperor; none held up, and he kowtowed to expose his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝察其不阿，欲大用，拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: The emperor saw that he would not flatter and wished to employ him greatly, appointing him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he would not flatter, the emperor wished to promote him greatly and made him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語輔臣，有無人才之歎，宗孟率爾對曰：「人才半為司馬光邪說所壞。」

translations.literal: The emperor once told his chief ministers that he lamented the lack of talent; Zongmeng blurted out: "Half our talent has been ruined by the heterodox doctrines of Sima Guang."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told his chief ministers he lacked talent. Zongmeng blurted: "Half our talent has been ruined by Sima Guang's heterodox doctrines."

sentences.zh: 帝不語，直視久之，曰：「蒲宗孟乃不取司馬光邪？

translations.literal: The emperor did not speak, stared at him a long time, and said: "Does Pu Zongmeng not esteem Sima Guang?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent, stared at him a long time, and said: "Does Pu Zongmeng look down on Sima Guang?

sentences.zh: 未論別事，只辭樞密一節，朕自即位以來，唯見此一人；

translations.literal: Leaving other matters aside, in the matter of declining the Bureau of Military Affairs alone, since I took the throne I have seen only this one man;
translations.idiomatic: Never mind other things—in declining the Bureau of Military Affairs alone, since I took the throne I have seen only this one man;

sentences.zh: 他人，則雖迫之使去，亦不肯矣。」

translations.literal: as for others, even if forced to leave they would not consent."
translations.idiomatic: as for others, even if you forced them out they would not go."

sentences.zh: 宗孟慚懼，至無以為容。

translations.literal: Zongmeng was ashamed and afraid, until he had no place to put himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmeng was ashamed and afraid, utterly abashed.

sentences.zh: 僅一歲，御史論其荒於酒色及繕治府舍過制，罷知汝州。

translations.literal: Barely a year later, censors attacked his dissipation in wine and women and his overbuilding of the prefectural residence; he was dismissed to know Run prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a year later censors attacked his dissipation in wine and women and his overbuilt prefectural residence; he was sent out as prefect of Run.

sentences.zh: 逾年，加資政殿學士，徙、杭、鄆三州。

translations.literal: After a year he was made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and transferred through Yi, Hang, and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and served in Yi, Hang, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 鄆介梁山濼，素多盜，宗孟痛治之，雖小偷微罪，亦斷其足筋，盜雖為衰止，而所殺亦不可勝計矣。

translations.literal: Yan bordered Liangshan marsh and had always had many bandits. Zongmeng punished them severely; even petty thieves with minor offenses had their leg tendons cut. Though banditry declined, those killed were also beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yan bordered Liangshan marsh and had always been full of bandits. Zongmeng punished them harshly; even petty thieves had their leg tendons severed. Banditry did decline, but the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 方徙河中，御史以慘酷劾，奪職知虢州。

translations.literal: Just as he was transferred to Hezhong, censors impeached him for cruelty and stripped his rank, making him prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: As he was transferred to Hezhong, censors impeached him for cruelty, stripped his rank, and made him prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 明年，復知河中，還其職。

translations.literal: The next year he again knew Hezhong and had his rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to Hezhong and had his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 帥永興，移大名。

translations.literal: He commanded Yongxing and moved to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Yongxing, then moved to Daming.

sentences.zh: 宗孟厭苦易地，頗默默不樂，復求河中。

translations.literal: Zongmeng wearied of constant transfers, grew silent and unhappy, and again asked for Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wearied of constant transfers, Zongmeng grew silent and unhappy and again asked for Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 宗孟趣尚嚴整而性侈汰，藏帑豐，每旦刲羊十、豕十，然燭三百入郡舍。

translations.literal: Zongmeng's tastes were severe and orderly but his nature extravagant; his treasury was rich. Each morning he slaughtered ten sheep and ten pigs and burned three hundred candles in the prefectural residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmeng was severe in manner but extravagant by nature. His treasury was rich. Each morning he slaughtered ten sheep and ten pigs and burned three hundred candles in the prefectural residence.

sentences.zh: 或請損之，慍曰：「君欲使我坐暗室忍饑邪？」

translations.literal: When someone asked him to reduce this, he said angrily: "Do you wish me to sit in a dark room and endure hunger?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked him to cut back, he snapped: "Do you want me to sit in the dark and starve?"

sentences.zh: 常日盥潔，有小洗面、大洗面、小濯足、大濯足、小大澡浴之別。

translations.literal: Daily washing had small face-washing, large face-washing, small foot-washing, large foot-washing, and small and large bathing.
translations.idiomatic: His daily ablutions distinguished small face-washing, large face-washing, small foot-washing, large foot-washing, and small and large bathing.

sentences.zh: 每用婢子數人，一浴至湯五斛。

translations.literal: Each time he used several maidservants; one bath used up to five hu of hot water.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he used several maidservants; one bath consumed up to five hu of hot water.

sentences.zh: 他奉養率稱是。

translations.literal: His other maintenance was mostly on this scale.
translations.idiomatic: His other upkeep was mostly on the same scale.

sentences.zh: 嘗以書抵蘇軾云：「晚年學道有所得。」

translations.literal: He once wrote to Su Shi, saying: "In my later years I have studied the Way and gained something."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote to Su Shi: "In my later years I have studied the Way and gained something."

sentences.zh: 軾答之曰：「聞所得甚高，然有二事相勸：一曰慈，二曰儉也。」

translations.literal: Shi answered: "I hear your attainment is very lofty, yet I have two things to urge upon you: first compassion, second frugality."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi replied: "I hear your attainment is very lofty, yet I urge two things upon you: compassion and frugality."

sentences.zh: 蓋針其失云。

translations.literal: This was to needle his faults.
translations.idiomatic: This was to needle his faults.

sentences.zh: 黃履，字安中，邵武人。

translations.literal: Huang Lu, styled Anzhong, was a man of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Lu, styled Anzhong, was from Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 少遊太學，舉進士，調南京法曹，又為高密、廣平王二宮教授、館閣校勘，同知禮院。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the Imperial University, passed the examinations, was appointed legal officer at Nanjing, then instructor to the princes of Gaomi and Guangping, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and associate director of the Court of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied at the Imperial University, passed the examinations, served as legal officer at Nanjing, then instructor to the princes of Gaomi and Guangping, collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and associate director of the Court of Rites.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史裏行，辭御史，改崇政殿說書兼知諫院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to investigating censor in waiting, declined the censorate, and was made lecturer at Chongzheng Hall while knowing the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to investigating censor in waiting, he declined the censorate and was made lecturer at Chongzheng Hall while directing the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘗詢天地合祭是非，對曰：「國朝之制，冬至祭天圓丘，夏至祭地方澤，每歲行之，皆合於古。

translations.literal: Shenzong once asked whether combined sacrifice of Heaven and Earth was right or wrong. He answered: "Our dynasty's system sacrifices Heaven at the round mound at the winter solstice and Earth at the square marsh at the summer solstice, each year—both accord with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong once asked whether the combined sacrifice of Heaven and Earth was correct. Lu answered: "Our dynasty sacrifices Heaven at the round mound at the winter solstice and Earth at the square marsh at the summer solstice each year—both accord with antiquity.

sentences.zh: 猶以有司攝事未足以盡，於是三歲一郊而親行之，所謂因時制宜者也，雖施之方今，為不可易。

translations.literal: Because officials acting as proxies is still not fully sufficient, every three years there is a suburban sacrifice performed in person—what is called adapting to the times. Though applied today, it cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Because proxy sacrifice by officials is still insufficient, every three years the emperor performs the suburban sacrifice in person—adapting to the times. Even today that cannot easily be changed.

sentences.zh: 惟合祭之非，在所當正。

translations.literal: Only the error of combined sacrifice is what must be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Only the error of combined sacrifice must be corrected.

sentences.zh: 然今日禮文之失，非獨此也，願敕有司正群祀，為一代損益之制。」

translations.literal: Yet today's ritual errors are not this alone; I wish Your Majesty to order the offices to correct all sacrifices and make a system of additions and subtractions for one generation."
translations.idiomatic: Yet today's ritual errors are not this alone. I ask Your Majesty to order the offices to correct all sacrifices and establish a ritual system for the age."

sentences.zh: 詔置局詳定，命履董之，北郊之議遂定。

translations.literal: An edict established a bureau to detail the matter, ordered Lu to direct it, and the northern suburban debate was settled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict established a bureau to work it out, with Lu in charge, and the northern suburban debate was settled.

sentences.zh: 同修起居注，進知制誥、同修國史。

translations.literal: He was co-compiler of the diary, advanced to drafter of edicts and co-compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was co-compiler of the diary, then advanced to drafter of edicts and co-compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂去，服除，以禮部尚書召。

translations.literal: He left on his mother's mourning; when mourning ended he was summoned as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He left to mourn his mother. When mourning ended he was summoned as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時閩中患苦鹽法，獻言者眾，神宗謂履自閩來，恃以為決。

translations.literal: At that time Fujian suffered under the salt law and many offered advice. Shenzong said that because Lu came from Fujian he would rely on him to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian was suffering under the salt law and many offered advice. Shenzong said that because Lu came from Fujian he would rely on him to decide.

sentences.zh: 履乃陳法甚便，遂不復革，鄉論鄙之。

translations.literal: Lu then declared the law very convenient and it was not reformed; local opinion despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu declared the law very convenient, so it was not reformed, and local opinion despised him.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was moved to chief investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 履以大臣多因細故罰金，遂言：「賈誼有云：『遇之以禮，則群臣自喜。』

translations.literal: Because many great ministers were fined for trifles, Lu said: "Jia Yi said: 'Treat them with ritual, and the ministers will rejoice themselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Because many great ministers were fined for trifles, Lu said: "Jia Yi said: 'Treat them with ritual, and the ministers will rejoice.'

sentences.zh: 群臣且然，況大臣乎？

translations.literal: If ministers are so, how much more great ministers?
translations.idiomatic: If that is true of ministers, how much more of great ministers?

sentences.zh: 使罪在可議，黜之可也；

translations.literal: If the offense is debatable, dismiss them;
translations.idiomatic: If the offense is debatable, dismiss them;

sentences.zh: 可恕，釋之可也，豈可罰以示辱哉！」

translations.literal: if pardonable, release them—how can you fine them to show humiliation!"
translations.idiomatic: if pardonable, release them. How can you fine them to humiliate them!"

sentences.zh: 時又制侍郎以下不許獨對，履言：「陛下博訪萬務，雖遠外微官，猶令獨對，顧於侍從乃弗得願也。」

translations.literal: At that time it was also decreed that vice directors and below might not have private audiences. Lu said: "Your Majesty broadly inquires into all affairs; though a distant minor official may still have a private audience, yet for attendants-in-waiting it is not granted."
translations.idiomatic: It was also decreed that vice directors and below might not have private audiences. Lu said: "Your Majesty inquires broadly into all affairs. Even distant minor officials may have private audiences, yet attendants-in-waiting may not speak as they wish."

sentences.zh: 遂刊其制。

translations.literal: The regulation was therefore struck.
translations.idiomatic: The regulation was struck.

sentences.zh: 御史翟思言事，有旨詰所自來。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Zhai Si spoke on affairs; an edict demanded where it came from.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Zhai Si spoke on policy; an edict demanded where his information came from.

sentences.zh: 履諫曰：「御史以言為職，非有所聞，則無以言。

translations.literal: Lu remonstrated: "Censors take speech as their duty; if they have heard nothing, they have nothing to say.
translations.idiomatic: Lu remonstrated: "Censors take speech as their duty. Without hearing something, they have nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 今乃究其自來，則人將懲之，臺諫不復有聞矣，恐失開言路之意。」

translations.literal: Now to investigate where it came from, people will restrain themselves and the censorate and remonstrance bureau will have no more reports—I fear this loses the intent of opening the path of speech."
translations.idiomatic: Now to trace their sources, people will restrain themselves and the censorate will fall silent—I fear this defeats opening the path of speech."

sentences.zh: 事乃寢。

translations.literal: The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，徙為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended the throne, Lu was transferred as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong ascended the throne, Lu was transferred as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 履素與蔡確、章惇、邢恕相交結，每確、惇有所嫌惡，則使恕道風旨於履，履即排擊之。

translations.literal: Lu had long been allied with Cai Que, Zhang Dun, and Xing Shu. Whenever Que or Dun hated someone, they would have Shu convey their intent to Lu, and Lu would attack the target.
translations.idiomatic: Lu had long been allied with Cai Que, Zhang Dun, and Xing Shu. Whenever Que or Dun hated someone, they would have Shu convey their intent to Lu, and Lu would attack the target.

sentences.zh: 至是，更自謂有定策功。

translations.literal: By this time he further claimed merit for deciding who would succeed.
translations.idiomatic: By this time he further claimed merit for deciding who would succeed.

sentences.zh: 劉安世發其罪，以龍圖閣直學士知越州，坐舉御史不當，降天章閣待制。

translations.literal: Liu Anshi exposed his crimes; he was made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Yuezhou. For improperly recommending a censor he was demoted to attendant academician of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anshi exposed his crimes; he was made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Yuezhou. For improperly recommending a censor he was demoted to attendant academician of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation.

sentences.zh: 歷舒、洪、蘇、鄂、青州、江寧、應天、潁昌府。

translations.literal: He served successively at Shu, Hong, Su, E, Qing, Jiangning, Yingtian, and Yingchang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively at Shu, Hong, Su, E, Qing, Jiangning, Yingtian, and Yingchang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，復龍圖閣直學士，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he was restored as direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made chief investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaosheng he was restored as direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made chief investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 極論呂大防、劉摯、梁燾垂簾時事，乞正典刑；

translations.literal: He fiercely argued the regency affairs of Lu Dafang, Liu Zhi, and Liang Tao, and begged that statutory punishment be applied;
translations.idiomatic: He fiercely argued the regency affairs of Lu Dafang, Liu Zhi, and Liang Tao, and begged that statutory punishment be applied;

sentences.zh: 又言司馬光變更先朝已行之法為罪。

translations.literal: and also said that Sima Guang was guilty for changing laws already in force under the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: and also said that Sima Guang was guilty for changing laws already in force under the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 先是，北郊之論雖定，猶不果行，履又建言：「陽復陰消，各因其時。

translations.literal: Earlier, though the northern suburban debate was settled, it had still not been carried out. Lu again memorialized: "Yang returns and yin recedes, each according to its season.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, though the northern suburban debate was settled, it had not been carried out. Lu memorialized again: "Yang returns and yin recedes, each in its season.

sentences.zh: 上圓下方，各順其體。

translations.literal: Heaven is round, earth square—each follows its form.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is round, earth square—each follows its form.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人因天祀天，因地祀地，三代至漢，其儀不易。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage sacrifices to Heaven because of Heaven and to Earth because of Earth; from the Three Dynasties to Han the rites did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore sages sacrifice to Heaven because of Heaven and to Earth because of Earth. From the Three Dynasties to Han the rites did not change.

sentences.zh: 及王莽諂事元后，遂躋地位，同席共牢，歷世襲行，不能全革。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang flattered the Empress Dowager Yuan, he raised her station, shared mat and food with her, and for generations the practice was inherited without full reform.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang flattered Empress Dowager Yuan, he raised her station and shared mat and food with her. For generations the practice continued without full reform.

sentences.zh: 逮神宗考古揆今，以正大典，嘗有意於茲矣。

translations.literal: When Shenzong examined antiquity and measured the present to rectify the great rites, he once had intent in this matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong examined antiquity and measured the present to rectify the great rites, he once intended this.

sentences.zh: 今承先志，當在陛下及二三執政。」

translations.literal: Now inheriting the late emperor's will, it lies with Your Majesty and two or three chief administrators."
translations.idiomatic: Now, inheriting the late emperor's will, it lies with Your Majesty and two or three chief administrators."

sentences.zh: 哲宗詢諸朝，章惇以為北郊止可謂之社。

translations.literal: Zhezong asked the court; Zhang Dun held that the northern suburban rite could only be called the earth sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong asked the court. Zhang Dun held that the northern suburban rite could only be called the earth sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 履曰：「天子祭天地。

translations.literal: Lu said: "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Lu said: "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 蓋郊者交於神明之義，所以天地皆稱郊。

translations.literal: For suburban sacrifice means communion with the spirits; therefore both Heaven and Earth are called suburban.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice means communion with the spirits; therefore both Heaven and Earth are called suburban.

sentences.zh: 故《詩序》云『郊祀天地』。

translations.literal: Thus the "Preface to the Odes" says "suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Preface to the Odes says "suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 若夫社者，土之神而已，豈有祭大祇亦謂之社乎？」

translations.literal: As for the earth sacrifice, it is only the spirit of soil—how can sacrificing to the great earth-spirit also be called the earth sacrifice?"
translations.idiomatic: The earth sacrifice is only to the spirit of soil. How can sacrificing to the great earth-spirit also be called the earth sacrifice?"

sentences.zh: 哲宗可之，遂定郊議。

translations.literal: Zhezong approved, and the suburban debate was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong approved, and the suburban debate was settled.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會正言鄒浩以言事貶新州，履曰：「浩以親被拔擢之故，敢犯顏納忠，陛下遽斥之死地，人臣將視以為戒，誰復敢為陛下論得失乎？

translations.literal: When Remonstrator Zou Hao was demoted to Xin prefecture for speaking out, Lu said: "Hao, because he was personally raised and promoted, dared to offend your countenance and offer loyal counsel. Your Majesty suddenly cast him to a deadly place; ministers will take this as a warning—who will again dare discuss gain and loss for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrator Zou Hao was demoted to Xin for speaking out, Lu said: "Hao, personally raised by you, dared to speak loyal truth. Your Majesty cast him to a deadly place. Ministers will take warning—who will dare discuss policy with you again?

sentences.zh: 乞徙善地。」

translations.literal: I beg he be moved to a better place."
translations.idiomatic: I beg he be moved to a better place."

sentences.zh: 坐罷知亳州。

translations.literal: For this he was dismissed to know Bo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was dismissed to Bo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，召為資政殿學士兼侍讀，復拜右丞。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne he was summoned as academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and attendant reader, and again made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne he was summoned as academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and attendant reader, and again made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 未逾年，求去，加大學士、提舉中太一宮，卒。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed he asked to leave, was given the grand academician title and made director of the Central Grand Unity Palace, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year passed he asked to leave, was given the grand academician title and made director of the Central Grand Unity Palace, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：哲宗親政之初，見慮未定，范、呂諸賢在廷，左右弼謨，俾日邇忠讜，疏絕回遹，以端其志向，元祐之治業，庶可守也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: At the beginning of Zhezong's personal rule, his views were not yet settled. Fan, Lu, and other worthies were at court, assisting left and right, drawing him daily toward loyal remonstrance, keeping devious paths at a distance to set his orientation—the achievements of Yuanyou governance might have been preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: When Zhezong first took personal rule his views were unsettled. Fan, Lu, and other worthies were at court, guiding him daily toward loyal remonstrance and shutting out devious paths—the Yuanyou achievement might have been preserved.

sentences.zh: 清臣怙才躁進，陰覬柄用，首發紹述之說，以隙國是，群奸洞之，衝決莫障，重為薦紳之禍焉。

translations.literal: Qingchen, relying on talent and rushing forward, secretly coveted power, first launched the doctrine of continuing the late emperor's policies, split the national consensus, and the whole pack of villains saw the gap and burst through without barrier, again bringing calamity to the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen, relying on talent and rushing ahead, secretly coveted power and first launched the doctrine of "continuing the late emperor's work," splitting national consensus. Villains saw the gap and burst through, bringing calamity again on the gentry.

sentences.zh: 至於興大獄以傾馮京、蘇軾者，璪也；

translations.literal: As for launching great prosecutions to overthrow Feng Jing and Su Shi—that was Zao;
translations.idiomatic: Launching great prosecutions to overthrow Feng Jing and Su Shi—that was Zao;

sentences.zh: 助成手實之法，以壞人材、讕司馬光者，宗孟也；

translations.literal: helping complete the household inventory law to ruin talent and slander Sima Guang—that was Zongmeng;
translations.idiomatic: helping complete the household inventory law to ruin talent and slander Sima Guang—that was Zongmeng;

sentences.zh: 訐垂簾之事，擊呂大防、劉摯等去之者，履也。

translations.literal: denouncing the regency, striking Lu Dafang, Liu Zhi, and others from office—that was Lu.
translations.idiomatic: denouncing the regency and driving Lu Dafang, Liu Zhi, and others from office—that was Lu.

sentences.zh: 清臣真小人之靡，三子抑其亞乎。

translations.literal: Qingchen was truly the dregs of petty men; were the three sons not next below him?
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen was truly the dregs of petty men; the three were perhaps next below him.

sentences.zh: 燾論議識趣，有可稱述，雖立朝無附，而依違蔡確、章惇間，無所匡建，非大臣之道也。

translations.literal: Dao's discourse and insight had points worth recounting. Though he stood at court without faction, he wavered between Cai Que and Zhang Dun and accomplished nothing to rectify or build—this was not the way of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Dao's discourse and insight had points worth recounting. Though he stood without faction, he wavered between Cai Que and Zhang Dun and built nothing—this was not the way of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 蔡挺，字子政，宋城人。

translations.literal: Cai Ting, styled Zizheng, was a man of Songcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ting, styled Zizheng, was from Songcheng.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調虔州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations and was appointed investigating officer of Qian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations and was appointed investigating officer of Qian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，以父希言當官蜀，乞代行，遂授陵州團練推官。

translations.literal: When his term ended, because his father Xiyan was to take office in Shu, he begged to go in his stead and was appointed investigating officer of Ling prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, because his father Xiyan was to take office in Shu, he begged to go in his stead and was appointed investigating officer of Ling.

sentences.zh: 王堯臣安撫陝西，辟管勾文字。

translations.literal: Wang Yaochen pacified Shaanxi and recruited him to manage documents.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yaochen pacified Shaanxi and recruited him to manage documents.

sentences.zh: 富弼使遼，奏挺從，至雄州，誓書有所更易，遣挺還白。

translations.literal: When Fu Bi went as envoy to Liao, he memorialized that Ting accompany him. At Xiong prefecture the oath document was somewhat changed; Ting was sent back to report.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Bi went as envoy to Liao, he asked Ting to accompany him. At Xiong the oath document was changed; Ting was sent back to report.

sentences.zh: 仁宗欲知契丹事，召對便殿，挺時有父喪，聽以衫帽入。

translations.literal: Renzong wished to know Liao affairs and summoned him to audience in the side hall. Ting was then in mourning for his father and was allowed to enter in shirt and cap.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong wished to know about Liao and summoned him to the side hall. Ting was in mourning for his father and was allowed to enter in shirt and cap.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹宣撫陝西、河東，奏挺通判涇州，徙鄜州。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan pacified Shaanxi and Hedong and memorialized Ting as vice prefect of Jing, then moved him to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan pacified Shaanxi and Hedong and had Ting made vice prefect of Jing, then moved him to Yan.

sentences.zh: 河北多盜，精擇諸郡守，以挺知博州。

translations.literal: Hebei had many bandits; the court carefully chose prefects and made Ting prefect of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei had many bandits; the court carefully chose prefects and made Ting prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 申飭屬縣嚴保伍，得居停奸盜者數人，弛其宿負，補為吏，使之察警，盜每發輒得。

translations.literal: He admonished the subordinate counties to enforce the mutual-responsibility groups strictly, found several who harbored bandits, released their old debts, made them clerks, and had them watch and report; whenever bandits struck they were caught.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered subordinate counties to enforce mutual-responsibility groups strictly, found several who harbored bandits, released their old debts, made them clerks to watch and report, and bandits were caught whenever they struck.

sentences.zh: 均博平、聊城二縣稅，歲衍鉅萬，三司下其法於四方，然大抵增賦也。

translations.literal: He equalized taxes in Boping and Liaocheng counties; each year they increased by tens of thousands, and the Three Departments sent the method to all circuits—but mostly it increased levies.
translations.idiomatic: He equalized taxes in Boping and Liaocheng counties, adding tens of thousands each year. The Three Departments spread the method everywhere, but it mostly increased levies.

sentences.zh: 為開封府推官、提點府界公事。

translations.literal: He was made investigating officer of Kaifeng prefecture and commissioner for metropolitan circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became investigating officer of Kaifeng and commissioner for metropolitan circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 部修六漯河，用李仲昌議，塞北流，入於六漯。

translations.literal: He supervised repair of the Six Luo River, using Li Zhongchang's proposal to block the northern flow and divert it into the Six Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised repair of the Six Luo River, using Li Zhongchang's plan to block the northern channel and divert it into the Six Luo.

sentences.zh: 一夕復決，兵夫芟楗漂溺不可計。

translations.literal: In one night it burst again; laborers cutting brush were swept away beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Overnight it burst again. Laborers cutting brush were swept away beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 降知滁州，言者以為輕，乃貶秩停官。

translations.literal: He was demoted to know Chuzhou; remonstrators thought it too light, so his rank was reduced and office suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Chuzhou. Critics thought the punishment too light, so his rank was cut and office suspended.

sentences.zh: 越數歲，稍起知南安軍，提點江西刑獄，提舉虔州鹽。

translations.literal: After several years he was slightly restored to know Nan'an army, commissioner for Jiangxi judicial matters, and director of Qianzhou salt.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was restored to Nan'an army, Jiangxi judicial commissioner, and director of Qianzhou salt.

sentences.zh: 自大庾嶺下南至廣，驛路荒遠，室廬稀疏，往來無所芘。

translations.literal: South from Dayu Ridge to Guang, the post road was desolate and houses sparse; travelers had nowhere to shelter.
translations.idiomatic: South from Dayu Ridge to Guang the post road was desolate and houses sparse; travelers had nowhere to shelter.

sentences.zh: 挺兄抗時為廣東轉運使，乃相與謀，課民植松夾道，以休行者。

translations.literal: Ting's elder brother Kang was then transport commissioner of Guangdong; they planned together to levy the people to plant pines along the road to shade travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's brother Kang was Guangdong transport commissioner. Together they had people plant pines along the road to shade travelers.

sentences.zh: 江閩鹽賊率千百為州縣害，挺諭所部與期，使首納器甲，原其罪，得兵械萬計。

translations.literal: Salt bandits of Jiang and Min gathered by the hundreds to harm prefectures and counties. Ting instructed his districts to set a deadline for surrender of weapons and armor, pardoned their crimes, and obtained tens of thousands of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Salt bandits in Jiang and Min gathered by the hundreds to plague the region. Ting set a deadline for surrender of arms, pardoned offenders, and collected tens of thousands of weapons.

sentences.zh: 官鹽惡而價貴，盜鹽善而價且下，故私販日滋。

translations.literal: Official salt was poor and costly; smuggled salt was good and cheaper—hence private trade daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Official salt was poor and costly while smuggled salt was better and cheaper, so private trade grew daily.

sentences.zh: 挺簡僚吏至淮轉新鹽，明殿賞，以官數之餘畀之，於是賊黨破散，宿弊遂絕，歲增賣鹽四十萬。

translations.literal: Ting selected subordinates to transport new salt from Huai, clarified rewards, and gave them the surplus beyond the official quota; thus the bandit gangs broke up, old abuses ended, and annual salt sales rose by four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ting sent officials to bring new salt from Huai, clarified rewards, and let them keep surplus beyond quota. Bandit gangs broke up, old abuses ended, and annual sales rose four hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 改陝西轉運副使，進直龍圖閣、知慶州，因上書論攻守大計。

translations.literal: He was made vice transport commissioner of Shaanxi, advanced to direct attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qing, and memorialized on grand strategy of attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Made Shaanxi vice transport commissioner, he advanced to Dragon Diagram attendant and prefect of Qing, and memorialized on grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 夏人大入，挺盡斂邊戶入保，戒諸砦無出戰。

translations.literal: The Xia invaded in force; Ting gathered all border households into forts and ordered the garrisons not to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia invaded in force, Ting gathered border households into forts and ordered garrisons not to fight.

sentences.zh: 諒祚親帥軍數萬攻大順，挺料城堅不可破，而柔遠城惡，亟遣總管張玉將銳師守之。

translations.literal: Liangzuo personally led tens of thousands to attack Dashun. Ting judged the city strong and unbreakable but Rouyuan weak, and urgently sent commander Zhang Yu with elite troops to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo led tens of thousands against Dashun. Ting judged Dashun strong but Rouyuan weak and urgently sent Zhang Yu with elite troops.

sentences.zh: 先布鐵蒺藜大順城旁水中，騎渡水多躓，驚言有神。

translations.literal: He first laid iron caltrops in the water beside Dashun; cavalry crossing stumbled and cried that spirits were at work.
translations.idiomatic: He laid iron caltrops in the water by Dashun. Cavalry stumbled crossing and cried that spirits were at work.

sentences.zh: 過三日不克，諒祚督帳下決戰，挺伏強弩壕外，飛矢貫其鎧，遂引卻。

translations.literal: After three days without success, Liangzuo urged his tent guards to decisive battle; Ting ambushed strong crossbows outside the moat, arrows piercing his armor, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After three days Liangzuo pressed for battle. Ting's crossbow ambush pierced his armor and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 移寇柔遠，玉夜斫營，夏人驚擾潰去。

translations.literal: Shifting the attack to Rouyuan, Yu raided the camp by night and the Xia fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: When the attack shifted to Rouyuan, Yu raided the camp at night and the Xia fled.

sentences.zh: 環州熟羌思順舉族投諒祚，倚為鄉導。

translations.literal: Sishun of Huan prefecture, a mature Qiang, led his clan to Liangzuo and served as guide.
translations.idiomatic: The mature Qiang Sishun of Huan led his clan to Liangzuo and served as guide.

sentences.zh: 挺宣言思順且復來，命葺其舊舍，出兵西為迎候之舉。

translations.literal: Ting proclaimed that Sishun would return, ordered his old house repaired, and sent troops west as if to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Ting proclaimed Sishun would return, repaired his house, and sent troops west as if to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 諒祚果疑思順，毒之死。

translations.literal: Liangzuo indeed suspected Sishun and poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo suspected Sishun and had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 挺築城馬練平為荔原堡，分屬羌三千人守之。

translations.literal: Ting built a city at Malianping as Liyuan fort and assigned three thousand Qiang to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Ting built Liyuan fort at Malianping and assigned three thousand Qiang to guard it.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，加天章閣待制、知渭州。

translations.literal: When Shenzong took the throne, Ting was made attendant of the Heavenly Manifest Hall and prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, Ting was made Heavenly Manifest attendant and prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 舉籍禁兵悉還府，不使有隱占。

translations.literal: He registered all forbidden troops and returned them to the commandery, not allowing hidden claims.
translations.idiomatic: He registered all forbidden troops and returned them to the commandery, ending hidden claims.

sentences.zh: 建勤武堂，五日一訓之，偏伍鉦鼓之法甚備。

translations.literal: He built the Hall of Martial Diligence, trained every five days, with complete methods of platoon gongs and drums.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Hall of Martial Diligence and trained every five days with full platoon drum methods.

sentences.zh: 儲勁卒於行間，遇用奇，則別為一隊。

translations.literal: He kept crack troops in the ranks; when special tactics were needed, they formed a separate unit.
translations.idiomatic: He kept crack troops in the ranks; for special tactics they formed separate units.

sentences.zh: 甲兵整習，常若寇至。

translations.literal: Armor and weapons were drilled until it seemed the enemy might arrive at any moment.
translations.idiomatic: Armor and weapons were drilled as if the enemy might arrive at any moment.

sentences.zh: 又分義勇為伍番，番三千人，參正兵防秋與春，以八月、正月集，四十五日而罷，歲省粟帛、錢緡十三萬有奇。

translations.literal: He also divided the volunteer militia into five rotations of three thousand each to join regular troops in autumn and spring defense, assembling in the eighth and first months for forty-five days, saving more than one hundred thirty thousand in grain, silk, and cash.
translations.idiomatic: He divided militia into five rotations of three thousand to join regulars in autumn and spring defense for forty-five days, saving over 130,000 in grain, silk, and cash.

sentences.zh: 括並邊生地冒耕田千八百頃，募人佃種，以益邊儲。

translations.literal: He inventoried eighteen hundred qing of border wasteland falsely cultivated and recruited tenants to increase frontier stores.
translations.idiomatic: He inventoried 1,800 qing of falsely cultivated border wasteland and recruited tenants to fill frontier stores.

sentences.zh: 取邊民闌市蕃部田八千頃，以給弓箭手。

translations.literal: He took eight thousand qing of tribal land illegally traded by border people and gave it to archers.
translations.idiomatic: He reclaimed 8,000 qing of tribal land illegally traded on the border for archers.

sentences.zh: 又築城定戎軍為熙寧砦，開地二千頃，募卒三千人耕守之。

translations.literal: He also fortified Dingwu army as Xining garrison, opened two thousand qing, and recruited three thousand soldiers to farm and guard.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Dingwu as Xining garrison, opened 2,000 qing, and recruited 3,000 soldiers to farm and guard.

sentences.zh: 諜告夏人集胡盧河，挺出奇兵迎擊之。

translations.literal: Spies reported the Xia gathering at Hulu River; Ting sent a surprise force to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported Xia gathering at Hulu River; Ting sent a surprise force.

sentences.zh: 夏人潰，分諸將躡而討之，蕩其七族。

translations.literal: The Xia routed; he sent generals in pursuit and destroyed seven clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia routed; generals pursued and destroyed seven clans.

sentences.zh: 進右諫議大夫，賜金帛三千。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Remonstrator and given three thousand in gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrator and given 3,000 in gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 夏人復犯諸砦，環慶兵不能禦，挺遣張玉以萬人往解其圍。

translations.literal: The Xia again attacked the garrisons; Huan and Qing troops could not resist; Ting sent Zhang Yu with ten thousand to relieve the siege.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia attacked again; Huan and Qing could not resist; Ting sent Zhang Yu with 10,000 to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 慶州軍變，挺討平之，進龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: Qingzhou troops mutinied; Ting suppressed them and was promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou mutinied; Ting suppressed it and was promoted to Dragon Diagram direct academician.

sentences.zh: 廣銳卒徙營，眾憚遷，欲為亂，城中震擾，挺推斬首惡十九人，訖徙營。

translations.literal: Guangrui troops were to move camp; the men feared transfer and plotted mutiny; the city was shaken; Ting executed nineteen ringleaders and completed the move.
translations.idiomatic: Guangrui troops feared a camp move and plotted mutiny. Ting executed nineteen ringleaders and completed the transfer.

sentences.zh: 蕃部歲饑，以田質於弓箭手，過期輒沒。

translations.literal: Tribal districts had famine yearly; they pawned fields to archers, which were forfeited when overdue.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal districts pawned fields to archers in famine years; overdue pledges were forfeited.

sentences.zh: 挺為貸官錢，歲息什一，後遂推為蕃漢青苗、助役法。

translations.literal: Ting lent official money at ten percent yearly interest; this was later extended as the Qiang-Han green sprout and labor-exemption laws.
translations.idiomatic: Ting lent official money at ten percent interest, later extended as Qiang-Han green sprout and labor-exemption laws.

sentences.zh: 又自以意製渡河大索及兵械鐮槍，皆獲其用。

translations.literal: He also devised on his own great ropes for crossing rivers and military sickles and spears, all proving useful.
translations.idiomatic: He devised river-crossing ropes and military sickles and spears, all proving useful.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining he was made vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xining (1072) he was made vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝問挺涇原訓兵之法，召部將按於崇政殿，善之，下以為諸郡法。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about Ting's Jingyuan training methods; he summoned his officers to demonstrate at Chongzheng Hall; the emperor approved and made it the model for all commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about Jingyuan training. Ting's officers demonstrated at Chongzheng Hall; the emperor made it the model for all commands.

sentences.zh: 河州景思立戰死，帝開天章閣訪執政，挺請行。

translations.literal: Jing Sili died fighting at He prefecture; the emperor opened the Heavenly Manifest Hall to consult chief ministers; Ting asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sili died at He prefecture. The emperor consulted ministers; Ting asked to go.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此小事，不足煩卿。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is a small matter, not worth troubling you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is a small matter, not worth troubling you.

sentences.zh: 河朔有警，卿當行矣。」

translations.literal: When there is alarm in Hebei, you shall go."
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei is threatened, you shall go."

sentences.zh: 契丹議雲中地，挺請罷沿邊戍人，示以無事，因乞置三十七將，皆行其策。

translations.literal: The Khitan debated Yunzhong territory; Ting asked to withdraw border garrisons to show peace and begged to establish thirty-seven commands—all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan debated Yunzhong. Ting asked to withdraw border garrisons to show peace and establish thirty-seven commands—all adopted.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，奏事殿中，疾作而仆，帝親臨賜藥，罷為資政殿學士、判南京留司御史臺。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year he reported at court, fell ill and collapsed; the emperor personally visited and gave medicine, then dismissed him as academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and judge of the Nanjing branch censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh winter he collapsed at court. The emperor visited and gave medicine, then made him Assisting Governance academician and Nanjing censorate judge.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，薨，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng he died at sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng (1079) he died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書，諡曰敏肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Minister of Works with posthumous name Minsu ("Quick and Solemn").
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works with posthumous name Minsu.

sentences.zh: 挺譎而多知，人莫能窺其城府。

translations.literal: Ting was crafty and knowing; no one could fathom his inner mind.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was crafty and knowing; no one could read his mind.

sentences.zh: 初，為富弼、范仲淹客，頗泄其幾事於呂夷簡以自售。

translations.literal: Earlier, as client to Fu Bi and Fan Zhongyan, he leaked their plans to Lü Yijian to sell himself.
translations.idiomatic: As client to Fu Bi and Fan Zhongyan, he leaked their plans to Lü Yijian for advancement.

sentences.zh: 在渭久，鬱鬱不自聊，寓意詞曲，有「玉關人老」之歎。

translations.literal: Long at Wei, depressed and restless, he put feeling into song lyrics with the sigh "Jade Pass grows old."
translations.idiomatic: Long at Wei, depressed, he wrote lyrics with the sigh "Jade Pass grows old."

sentences.zh: 中使至，則使優伶歌之，以達於禁掖。

translations.literal: When palace envoys came, he had actors sing them to reach the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When palace envoys came, he had actors sing them to reach the inner court.

sentences.zh: 神宗湣焉，遂有樞密之拜云。

translations.literal: Shenzong pitied him and thus came the Bureau of Military Affairs appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong pitied him and thus came his Bureau appointment.

sentences.zh: 兄 抗 抗，字子直。

translations.literal: Elder brother Kang. Kang, styled Zizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Kang. Kang, styled Zizhi.

sentences.zh: 中進士，調太平州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations and was appointed investigating officer of Taiping prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating officer of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 聞父疾，委官去。

translations.literal: Hearing his father was ill, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his father was ill, he resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 稍遷睦親宅講書。

translations.literal: He was gradually moved to lecturer at the Mansion of Close Kin.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to lecturer at the Mansion of Close Kin.

sentences.zh: 英宗在宮邸，器重之，請於安懿王，願得與遊。

translations.literal: When Yingzong was in the palace residence he valued him, asked Prince Anyi, and wished to associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: While Yingzong was in the palace residence he valued Kang, asked Prince Anyi, and wished his company.

sentences.zh: 每見，必衣冠盡禮，義兼師友。

translations.literal: Each meeting he wore full dress and complete ritual, with the bond of teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they met he wore full court dress and treated him with the courtesy due to both teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常博士、通判秦州，為秘閣校理，乞知蘇州。

translations.literal: Again moved to Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices and vice prefect of Qin, made collator of the Secret Archive, and begged to know Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices and vice prefect of Qin, collator of the Secret Archive, and asked to be sent to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 州並江湖，民田苦風潮害，抗築長堤，自城屬昆山，亙八十里，民得立塍堨，大以為利。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered rivers and lakes; the people's fields suffered wind and tide harm; Kang built a long dike from the city to Kunshan, eighty li, so the people could build embankments—great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou bordered the lakes; fields suffered from wind and tides. Kang built an eighty-li dike to Kunshan so people could raise embankments—a great benefit.

sentences.zh: 徙廣東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 岑水銅冶廢，官給虛券為市，久不償。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guangdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 人無所取資，聚而私鑄，抗盡給之，人得直以止。

translations.literal: The Censhui copper works were abandoned; the government issued empty vouchers as currency long unpaid; people had no resources and gathered to coin privately; Kang paid all in full and private coining stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Censhui copper works were abandoned; empty vouchers went unpaid; people coined privately until Kang paid in full and coining stopped.

sentences.zh: 番禺歲運鹽英、韶，道遠，多侵竊雜惡。

translations.literal: Panyu yearly transported salt to Ying and Shao; the road was long and much was stolen or adulterated.
translations.idiomatic: Panyu shipped salt to Ying and Shao yearly; the road was long and much was stolen or adulterated.

sentences.zh: 抗命十舸為一運，擇攝官主之，歲終會其殿最，增十五萬緡。

translations.literal: Kang ordered ten boats per convoy with an acting official in charge; at year's end he reviewed performance and added one hundred fifty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Kang ordered ten boats per convoy with acting officials; year-end review added 150,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，召為三司判官。

translations.literal: When Yingzong took the throne he was summoned as judge of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong took the throne he was summoned as Three Departments judge.

sentences.zh: 廣部去京師遠，不即至，帝見南來者必問之。

translations.literal: Guang was far from the capital and he did not arrive promptly; the emperor asked every southerner he saw about him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was far from the capital; the emperor asked every southerner about him.

sentences.zh: 及入對，諭曰：「卿乃吾故人，朕望於卿者厚，勿以常禮自疏也。」

translations.literal: When he entered audience the emperor instructed: "You are my old acquaintance; I expect much of you—do not distance yourself with ordinary ritual."
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor said: "You are my old friend; I expect much—do not stand on ceremony."

sentences.zh: 以史館修撰同知諫院。

translations.literal: He was made historiographer and associate director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was made historiographer and associate remonstrance director.

sentences.zh: 方議安懿王典禮，抗引禮為人後之誼，指陳切至，涕淚被面，帝亦感泣。

translations.literal: When the rites for Prince Anyi were debated, Kang cited the ritual of becoming another's heir, arguing to the point with tears on his face; the emperor wept as well.
translations.idiomatic: Debating Prince Anyi's rites, Kang cited adoption ritual with tears; the emperor wept too.

sentences.zh: 都城大水，抗請見，帝迎問之，抗推原變異，守前說以對。

translations.literal: The capital had great flood; Kang requested audience; the emperor received him and asked; Kang traced omens and held to his earlier view.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital flooded, Kang sought audience; the emperor received him; Kang traced omens and held his view.

sentences.zh: 大臣畏其諫列，白為知制誥，遷龍圖閣直學士、知定州。

translations.literal: Great ministers feared his remonstrance and had him made drafter of edicts and direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, knowing Ding prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers feared his remonstrance and made him edict drafter and Dragon Diagram academician at Ding.

sentences.zh: 帝惜其去，曰：「第行，且召矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor regretted his leaving and said: "Go for now—you will be recalled."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted his leaving: "Go for now—you will be recalled."

sentences.zh: 郡兵番戍，室家留營多不謹，夫歸輒首原，抗下令悉按以法，戍者感焉。

translations.literal: Commandery troops rotated garrison; families left in camp were often careless; when husbands returned they were first forgiven; Kang ordered all punished by law and the garrison men were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Rotating garrison troops left careless families; husbands were forgiven on return; Kang punished by law and the garrison was moved.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，趣命為太子詹事，未至而神宗立，改樞密直學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: The emperor fell ill and Kang was urgently made heir-apparent tutor; before he arrived Shenzong took the throne; he was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and prefect of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell ill and Kang was made heir-apparent tutor; before arrival Shenzong took the throne and made him bureau academician and Qin prefect.

sentences.zh: 過闕，帝見之，悲慟不自勝，曰：「先帝疾大漸，猶不忘卿。」

translations.literal: Passing the capital the emperor saw him, grief beyond control, saying: "When the late emperor was gravely ill he still did not forget you."
translations.idiomatic: Passing the capital the emperor saw him, grief-stricken: "When the late emperor was dying he still remembered you."

sentences.zh: 遂赴鎮。

translations.literal: He then went to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to his post.

sentences.zh: 秦有質院，質諸羌百餘人，自少至老，扃繫之，非死不出，抗皆縱釋，約毋得擅相仇殺。

translations.literal: Qin had a hostage compound holding over a hundred Qiang from youth to old age, locked in, not released until death; Kang released them all and forbade private vendettas.
translations.idiomatic: Qin held over a hundred Qiang hostages locked until death; Kang released them and forbade private vendettas.

sentences.zh: 已而有犯者，斬以徇，莫敢奸令。

translations.literal: When some violated this, he beheaded them as warning; none dared break the order.
translations.idiomatic: Violators were beheaded as warning; none dared break the order.

sentences.zh: 居數日，夢英宗召語，眷如平生，欲退復留。

translations.literal: After several days he dreamed Yingzong summoned him to talk with affection as in life, wishing to leave yet detained.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he dreamed Yingzong summoned him with affection as in life, wishing to leave yet detained.

sentences.zh: 覺為家人言，感念歔欷。

translations.literal: Awake he told his family and sighed with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Awake he told his family and sighed.

sentences.zh: 及靈駕發引之旦，東望號慟，見僚佐於便室，驟得疾卒，年六十。

translations.literal: On the morning the imperial coffin set out, he looked east and wailed; meeting aides in the side room he suddenly fell ill and died at sixty.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin set out he wailed eastward; meeting aides he suddenly fell ill and died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 特贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously given Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 又欲賜諡，吳奎曰：「抗以舊恩，自雜學士贈官，已逾常制。」

translations.literal: They also wished to grant a posthumous name; Wu Kui said: "Kang, through old favor, was given office from a miscellaneous academician—already beyond convention."
translations.idiomatic: They wished a posthumous name; Wu Kui said: "Kang was promoted from miscellaneous academician through old favor—already beyond convention."

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: It stopped.
translations.idiomatic: It stopped.

sentences.zh: 王韶，字子純，江州德安人。

translations.literal: Wang Shao, styled Zichun, was a man of De'an in Jiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, styled Zichun, was from De'an in Jiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調新安主簿、建昌軍司理參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations and was appointed registrar of Xin'an and judicial officer of Jianchang army.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations and was registrar of Xin'an and judicial officer of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 試制科不中，客遊陝西，訪采邊事。

translations.literal: He failed the special decree examination, traveled in Shaanxi as a guest, and gathered frontier intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the special decree exam, traveled Shaanxi, and gathered frontier intelligence.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，詣闕上《平戎策》三篇，其略以為：

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining he came to court and submitted three chapters of "Pacifying the Rong," the gist being:
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining he submitted three chapters of "Pacifying the Rong," arguing:

sentences.zh: 「西夏可取。

translations.literal: "Western Xia can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: "Western Xia can be taken.

sentences.zh: 欲取西夏，當先復河、湟，則夏人有腹背受敵之憂。

translations.literal: To take Western Xia, He and Huang must first be recovered, then the Xia will fear attack from front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: To take Western Xia, recover He and Huang first so the Xia fear attack from front and rear.

sentences.zh: 夏人比年攻青唐，不能克，萬一克之，必並兵南向，大掠秦、渭之間，牧馬於蘭、會，斷古渭境，盡服南山生羌，西築武勝，遣兵時掠洮、河，則隴、蜀諸郡當盡驚擾，瞎征兄弟其能自保邪？

translations.literal: The Xia in recent years attacked Qingtang without success; if they should take it they will surely unite forces southward, plunder Qin and Wei, pasture at Lan and Hui, cut off Gu Guwei, subdue all southern Qiang, build Wusheng in the west, and raid Tao and He—then Long and Shu commanderies will be alarmed; can the brothers of Zhezheng protect themselves?
translations.idiomatic: The Xia attacked Qingtang without success; if they took it they would march south, plunder Qin and Wei, cut Guwei, subdue Qiang, and alarm Long and Shu—could Zhezheng's brothers protect themselves?

sentences.zh: 今唃氏子孫，唯董氈粗能自立，瞎征、欺巴溫之徒，又法所及，各不過一二百里，其勢豈能與西人抗哉！

translations.literal: Of the Gu clan descendants only Dong Zhan can barely stand alone; Zhezheng, Qiba Wen, and the like are within reach, each no more than one or two hundred li—how can their strength resist the western enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Of the Gu clan only Dong Zhan stands alone; Zhezheng and Qiba Wen are within reach, each under two hundred li—how can they resist the western enemy!

sentences.zh: 武威之南，至於洮、河、蘭、鄯，皆故漢郡縣，所謂湟中、浩、大小榆、枹罕，土地肥美，宜五種者在焉。

translations.literal: South of Wuwei to Tao, He, Lan, and Shan—all former Han commanderies and counties, the so-called Huangzhong, Hao, large and small Yu, and Baohan—land fertile and fit for the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: South of Wuwei to Tao, He, Lan, and Shan lie former Han counties—Huangzhong, Hao, Yu, Baohan—fertile and fit for grain.

sentences.zh: 幸今諸羌瓜分，莫相統一，此正可並合而兼撫之時也。

translations.literal: Fortunately the Qiang are now divided without unity—this is the time to combine and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the Qiang are divided—now is the time to combine and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 諸種既服，唃氏敢不歸？

translations.literal: Once the tribes submit, will the Gu clan dare not return?
translations.idiomatic: Once the tribes submit, will the Gu clan not return?

sentences.zh: 唃氏歸則河西李氏在吾股掌中矣。

translations.literal: If the Gu clan returns, the Li clan of Hexi is in our palm.
translations.idiomatic: If the Gu clan returns, the Li of Hexi are in our palm.

sentences.zh: 且唃氏子孫，瞎征差盛，為諸羌所畏，若招諭之，使居武勝或渭源城，使糾合宗黨，制其部族，習用漢法，異時族類雖盛，不過一延州李士彬、環州慕恩耳。

translations.literal: Among Gu descendants Zhezheng is rather strong and feared by the Qiang; if summoned to dwell at Wusheng or Weiyuan, to gather clans and control tribes and learn Han ways, even if their kind grows strong later they will be no more than Li Shibin of Yanzhou or Mu En of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezheng is strong and feared; if settled at Wusheng or Weiyuan to gather clans and learn Han ways, they would be no more than Li Shibin or Mu En.

sentences.zh: 為漢有肘腋之助，且使夏人無所連結，策之上也。」

translations.literal: To give Han an arm at the elbow and leave the Xia without allies—this is the best strategy."
translations.idiomatic: To give Han an arm at the elbow and cut Xia alliances—this is the best strategy."

sentences.zh: 神宗異其言，召問方略，以韶管幹秦鳳經略司機宜文字。

translations.literal: Shenzong was struck by his words, summoned him to ask strategy, and made Shao manage documents for the Qinfeng circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong was struck by his words, summoned him, and made Shao staff officer for the Qinfeng commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蕃部俞龍珂在青唐最大，渭源羌與夏人皆欲羈屬之，諸將議先致討。

translations.literal: Tribal chief Yu Longke at Qingtang was largest; Weiyuan Qiang and Xia both wished to attach to him; generals debated attacking first.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Longke at Qingtang was the largest chief; Weiyuan Qiang and Xia both wanted him; generals debated attacking first.

sentences.zh: 韶因按邊，引數騎直抵其帳，諭其成敗，遂留宿。

translations.literal: Shao on inspection took several horsemen straight to his tent, explained success and failure, and stayed overnight.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection Shao took a few horsemen to Longke's tent, explained the odds, and stayed overnight.

sentences.zh: 明旦，兩種皆遣其豪隨以東。

translations.literal: At dawn both tribes sent their chiefs east with him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn both tribes sent chiefs east with him.

sentences.zh: 久之，龍珂率屬十二萬口內附，所謂包順者也。

translations.literal: After long time Longke led twelve myriad mouths to submit inward—the so-called Baoshun.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Longke led 120,000 people to submit—the so-called Baoshun.

sentences.zh: 韶又言：「渭源至秦州，良田不耕者萬頃，願置市易司，頗籠商賈之利，取其贏以治田。」

translations.literal: Shao also said: "From Weiyuan to Qin prefecture ten thousand qing of good fields lie uncultivated; I wish to establish a market monopoly office to capture merchant profit and use the surplus to work the fields."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "From Weiyuan to Qin, ten thousand qing of good land lie fallow. Establish a market office, capture merchant profit, and use surplus to farm."

sentences.zh: 帝從其言，改著作佐郎，仍命韶提舉。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and changed him to assistant compiler, still ordering Shao to direct it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, made him assistant compiler, and ordered him to direct it.

sentences.zh: 經略使李師中言：「韶乃欲指占極邊弓箭手地耳，又將移市易司於古渭，恐秦州自此益多事，所得不補所亡。」

translations.literal: Commissioner Li Shizhong said: "Shao only wishes to seize the archers' frontier land and move the market office to Guwei—fearing Qin will have more trouble and gain will not repay loss."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhong said: "Shao only wants archer land and to move the market office to Guwei—Qin will only suffer more trouble."

sentences.zh: 王安石主韶議，為罷師中，以竇舜卿代，且遣李若愚按實。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi backed Shao; Shizhong was dismissed, Dou Shunqing replaced him, and Li Ruoyu was sent to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi backed Shao; Shizhong was dismissed, Dou Shunqing replaced him, and Li Ruoyu was sent to verify.

sentences.zh: 若愚至，問田所在，韶不能對。

translations.literal: Ruoyu arrived and asked where the fields were; Shao could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoyu asked where the fields were; Shao could not answer.

sentences.zh: 舜卿檢索，僅得地一頃，既地主有訟，又歸之矣。

translations.literal: Shunqing searched and found only one qing; the landowner sued and it was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqing found only one qing; the owner sued and it was returned.

sentences.zh: 若愚奏其欺，安石又為罷舜卿而命韓縝。

translations.literal: Ruoyu memorialized the deception; Anshi again dismissed Shunqing and appointed Han Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoyu reported the fraud; Anshi dismissed Shunqing and appointed Han Zong.

sentences.zh: 縝遂附會實其事，師中、舜卿皆坐謫，而韶為太子中允、秘閣校理。

translations.literal: Zong then corroborated the matter; Shizhong and Shunqing were both demoted, and Shao was made palace attendant and collator.
translations.idiomatic: Zong corroborated the story; Shizhong and Shunqing were demoted; Shao became palace attendant and collator.

sentences.zh: 後帥郭逵上韶盜貸市易錢，安石以為不足校，徙逵涇原。

translations.literal: Later commander Guo Kui reported Shao embezzled market funds; Anshi thought it not worth investigating and moved Kui to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guo Kui reported Shao embezzled market funds; Anshi dismissed it and moved Kui to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝志復河、隴，築古渭為通遠軍，以韶知軍事。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to recover He and Long, built Guwei as Tongyuan army, and made Shao know its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to recover He and Long, built Guwei as Tongyuan army, and put Shao in charge.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，引兵城渭源堡及乞神平，破蒙羅角、抹耳水巴等族。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, seventh month, he led troops to fortify Weiyuan garrison and Qishenping, defeating the Mengluojiao and Mo'er Shuiba tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, seventh month, he fortified Weiyuan and Qishenping and defeated Mengluojiao and Mo'er Shuiba.

sentences.zh: 初，羌保險，諸將謀置陣平地，韶曰：「賊不舍險來鬥，則我師必徒歸。

translations.literal: At first the Qiang held the defiles; generals wished to array on flat ground. Shao said: "If the enemy will not leave the defiles to fight, our army returns empty.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang held defiles; generals wanted flat ground. Shao said: "If they will not leave the defiles, we march home empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 今已入險地，當使險為吾有。」

translations.literal: Now we have entered dangerous ground—we must make the danger ours."
translations.idiomatic: We are in dangerous ground—we must make it ours."

sentences.zh: 乃徑趣抹邦山，壓敵軍而陣，令曰：「敢言退者斬！」

translations.literal: He went straight to Mobang mountain, pressed the enemy army and arrayed, ordering: "Who speaks of retreat is beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: He went straight to Mobang, pressed the enemy, and ordered: "Who speaks of retreat dies!"

sentences.zh: 賊乘高下鬥，師小卻。

translations.literal: The enemy fought from high ground; the army slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fought from high ground; the army fell back slightly.

sentences.zh: 韶躬擐甲胃，麾帳下兵逆擊之，羌大潰，焚其廬帳而還，洮西大震。

translations.literal: Shao donned armor himself, commanded his guards to counterattack; the Qiang routed; they burned their tents and returned; Taoxi was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shao donned armor, counterattacked; the Qiang routed; they burned tents; Taoxi shook.

sentences.zh: 會瞎征度洮為之援，餘黨復集。

translations.literal: Zhezheng crossed Tao to aid them; remnant parties gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezheng crossed Tao to aid them; remnants gathered again.

sentences.zh: 韶命別將由竹牛嶺路張軍聲，而潛師越武勝，遇瞎征首領瞎藥等，與戰破之，遂城武勝，建為鎮洮軍。

translations.literal: Shao ordered another general to feign along Zhuniu Ridge while secretly crossing Wusheng, met Zhezheng's chiefs Xia Yao and others, defeated them, fortified Wusheng, and established Zhentao army.
translations.idiomatic: Shao feigned along Zhuniu Ridge while secretly crossing Wusheng, defeated Zhezheng's chiefs, fortified Wusheng, and established Zhentao army.

sentences.zh: 進右正言、集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Rectifier and academician of the Hall for Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Rectifier and Hall for Assembled Worthies academician.

sentences.zh: 復擊走瞎征，降其部落二萬。

translations.literal: He again drove off Zhezheng and received submission of twenty thousand of his tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He again drove off Zhezheng and received twenty thousand tribes.

sentences.zh: 更名鎮洮為熙州，以熙、河、洮、岷、通遠為一路，韶以龍圖閣待制知熙州。

translations.literal: Zhentao was renamed Xi prefecture; Xi, He, Tao, Min, and Tongyuan formed one circuit; Shao was made Dragon Diagram attendant and prefect of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhentao became Xi; Xi, He, Tao, Min, and Tongyuan formed one circuit; Shao was Dragon Diagram attendant and Xi prefect.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，取河州，遷樞密直學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, third month, he took He prefecture and was moved to direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, third month, he took He and became bureau direct academician.

sentences.zh: 降羌叛，韶回軍擊之。

translations.literal: Submitting Qiang rebelled; Shao turned the army to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Submitting Qiang rebelled; Shao turned to strike them.

sentences.zh: 瞎征以其間據河州，韶進破訶諾木藏城，穿露骨山，南入洮州境，道狹隘，釋馬徒行，或日至六七。

translations.literal: Zhezheng meanwhile seized He; Shao advanced, broke Henuo Mucang city, crossed Lougu mountain, south into Tao, the road narrow; he left horses and walked, sometimes six or seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezheng seized He; Shao broke Henuo Mucang, crossed Lougu, entered Tao on foot—sometimes six or seven days.

sentences.zh: 瞎征留其黨守河州，自將尾官軍，韶力戰破走之，河州復平。

translations.literal: Zhezheng left his party to hold He and personally trailed the army; Shao fought hard and drove him off; He was pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezheng left men at He and trailed the army; Shao drove him off and pacified He.

sentences.zh: 連拔宕、岷二州，疊、洮羌酋皆以城附。

translations.literal: He took Dang and Min in succession; Die and Tao chiefs all submitted their cities.
translations.idiomatic: He took Dang and Min; Die and Tao chiefs submitted their cities.

sentences.zh: 軍行五十有四日，涉千八百里，得州五，斬首數千級，獲牛、羊、馬以萬計。

translations.literal: The army marched fifty-four days, covered eighteen hundred li, gained five prefectures, beheaded several thousand, captured cattle, sheep, and horses by the myriad.
translations.idiomatic: In fifty-four days and 1,800 li he gained five prefectures, beheaded thousands, and captured myriad livestock.

sentences.zh: 進左諫議大夫、端明殿學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Remonstrator and academician of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Remonstrator and Bright Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 七年，入朝，又加資政殿學士，賜第崇仁坊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered court, was again given Assisting Governance academician, and granted a residence in Chongren ward.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he entered court, gained Assisting Governance academician, and a Chongren ward residence.

sentences.zh: 還至興平，聞景思立敗於踏白城，賊圍河州，日夜馳至熙。

translations.literal: Returning to Xingping he heard Jing Sili was defeated at Tabai, bandits besieged He; he raced day and night to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingping he heard Jing Sili fell at Tabai and He was besieged; he raced to Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙方城守，命撤之。

translations.literal: Xi was just fortifying; he ordered the walls dismantled.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was fortifying; he ordered the walls dismantled.

sentences.zh: 選兵得二萬。

translations.literal: He selected twenty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He selected twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 議所向，諸將欲趨河州。

translations.literal: Debating direction, the generals wished to hurry to He.
translations.idiomatic: Generals wished to hurry to He.

sentences.zh: 韶曰：「賊所以圍城者，恃有外援也。

translations.literal: Shao said: "The enemy besieges the city because they rely on outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "They besiege because they expect aid.

sentences.zh: 今知救至，必設伏待我，且新勝氣銳，未可與爭。

translations.literal: Now knowing rescue comes they will surely ambush us; fresh victory makes them sharp—we cannot fight yet.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing rescue comes they will ambush; fresh victory makes them sharp—we cannot fight yet.

sentences.zh: 當出其不意，以攻其所恃，此所謂『批亢搗虛，形格勢禁，則自為解』者也。」

translations.literal: We must strike where they do not expect, attack what they rely on—this is what is called striking the vitals to relieve the siege."
translations.idiomatic: Strike the unexpected, attack what they rely on—strike vitals to lift the siege."

sentences.zh: 乃直扣定羌城，破結河族，斷夏國通路，進臨寧河，分命偏將入南山。

translations.literal: He went straight to Dingqiang, broke the Jiehe tribe, cut Xia communications, advanced to Ninghe, and sent flank generals into the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Dingqiang, broke Jiehe, cut Xia communications, advanced to Ninghe, and sent flanks into the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 瞎征知援絕，拔柵去。

translations.literal: Zhezheng knew aid was cut and withdrew the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezheng knew aid was cut and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，思立之覆師也，羌勢復熾，朝廷議棄熙河，帝為之旰食，數下詔戒韶持重勿出。

translations.literal: At first when Sili's army was destroyed Qiang power revived; court debated abandoning Xihe; the emperor lost appetite and repeatedly ordered Shao to be cautious and not advance.
translations.idiomatic: After Sili's defeat Qiang revived; court debated abandoning Xihe; the emperor ordered Shao to hold back.

sentences.zh: 及是，帝大喜。

translations.literal: At this the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 韶還熙州，以兵循西山繞出踏白後，焚八千帳，瞎征窮蹙丐降，俘以獻。

translations.literal: Shao returned to Xi, took troops along the western mountains behind Tabai, burned eight thousand tents; Zhezheng in extremity begged surrender and was captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Shao returned to Xi, swept behind Tabai, burned eight thousand tents; Zhezheng surrendered and was captured.

sentences.zh: 拜韶觀文殿學士、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shao was made Observing Culture academician and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was made Observing Culture academician and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 資政、觀文學士，非嘗執政而除者，皆自韶始。

translations.literal: Assisting Governance and Observing Culture academics not previously given to non-chief ministers—all began with Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting Governance and Observing Culture titles for non-chief ministers—all began with Shao.

sentences.zh: 官其兄弟及兩子，前後賜絹八千匹。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his brothers and two sons; before and after he was given eight thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed brothers and two sons and received eight thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙河雖名一路，而實無租入，軍食皆仰給他道。

translations.literal: Xihe though called a circuit in fact had no rent; army food all depended on other routes.
translations.idiomatic: Xihe was called a circuit but had no rent; army food came from other routes.

sentences.zh: 轉運判官馬瑊捃官吏細故，韶欲罷瑊，王安石右瑊，韶始沮，於是與安石異。

translations.literal: Transport judge Ma Jian picked at officials' trifles; Shao wished to dismiss Jian; Anshi sided with Jian; Shao was discouraged and thus differed from Anshi.
