translations.idiomatic: Transport judge Ma Jian nitpicked officials; Shao wished to dismiss him; Anshi sided with Jian; Shao fell out with Anshi.

sentences.zh: 數以母老乞歸，帝語安石勉留之。

translations.literal: Several times he begged return because his mother was old; the emperor told Anshi to urge him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to return for his aged mother; the emperor told Anshi to keep him.

sentences.zh: 安南之役，韶言：「決里、廣源之建，臣以為貪虛名而忘實禍，執政乃疑臣為刺譏。

translations.literal: On the Annan campaign Shao said: "Establishing Jueli and Guangyuan I held was greed for empty fame and forgetting real harm; the administration suspected me of satire.
translations.idiomatic: On Annan Shao said: "Jueli and Guangyuan were empty fame forgetting real harm; the administration suspected satire.

sentences.zh: 方舉事之初，臣力爭極論，欲寬民力而省財用，但同列莫肯聽，至以熙河事折臣。

translations.literal: At the start I argued forcefully to ease the people and save funds, but colleagues would not listen, even using Xihe to refute me.
translations.idiomatic: At the start I argued to ease the people and save funds; colleagues would not listen and used Xihe against me.

sentences.zh: 臣本意不費朝廷而可以至伊吾盧甘，初不欲令熙河作路，河、岷作州也。

translations.literal: My intent was not to spend the court yet reach Yiwu and Lugan; I did not wish Xihe made a circuit or He and Min made prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: I meant not to spend the court yet reach Yiwu and Lugan; I did not want Xihe a circuit or He and Min prefectures.

sentences.zh: 今與眾異論，儻不求退，必致不容。」

translations.literal: Now I differ from the multitude; if I do not seek retirement I will surely be intolerable."
translations.idiomatic: Now I differ from others; if I do not retire I will be intolerable."

sentences.zh: 韶本鑿空開邊，驟躋政地，乃以勤兵費財歸曲朝廷，帝由是不悅，以故罷職知洪州，又坐謝表怨慢，落職知鄂州。

translations.literal: Shao had hollowed the frontier and suddenly risen to power; he now blamed the court for costly troops; the emperor was displeased and dismissed him to Hong, then for a thank-you memorial of resentment was demoted to E.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had opened the frontier and risen fast; he blamed the court for costly war; the emperor dismissed him to Hong, then to E for a resentful memorial.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，還其職，復知洪州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng his rank was restored and he again knew Hong.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng year two his rank was restored and he returned to Hong.

sentences.zh: 四年，病疽卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died of carbuncle at fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he died of carbuncle at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰襄敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grandee of Splendid Happiness with posthumous name Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given Grandee of Splendid Happiness, posthumous name Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 韶起孤生，用兵有機略。

translations.literal: Shao rose from a lone scholar; in using troops he had stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Shao rose alone; in war he had stratagem.

sentences.zh: 臨出師，召諸將授以指，不復更問，每戰必捷。

translations.literal: Before battle he summoned generals and gave instructions without further question; each battle was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle he instructed generals once; each battle he won.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜臥帳中，前部遇敵，矢石已交，呼聲震山谷，侍者往往股栗，而韶鼻息自如。

translations.literal: Once he slept in the tent while the vanguard met the enemy; arrows and stones crossed, shouts shook valleys; attendants often trembled in the thighs while Shao breathed as in sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Once while he slept in camp the vanguard fought; attendants trembled while Shao slept peacefully.

sentences.zh: 在鄂宴客，出家姬奏樂，客張繢醉挽一姬不前，將擁之，姬泣以告。

translations.literal: At E he feasted guests with household singers; guest Zhang Hui drunk pulled a girl who would not come forward and was about to embrace her; she wept and told Shao.
translations.idiomatic: At E he feasted with singers; drunk Zhang Hui pulled a girl who wept to Shao.

sentences.zh: 韶徐曰：「本出汝曹娛客，而令失歡如此。」

translations.literal: Shao said calmly: "They were meant to entertain you, yet you spoil the mood."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said calmly: "They were to entertain you, yet you spoil the mood."

sentences.zh: 命酌大杯罰之，談笑如故，人亦服其量。

translations.literal: He ordered a large cup to punish Hui and talked and laughed as before; people admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a large cup for Hui and laughed as before; people admired his breadth.

sentences.zh: 韶交親多楚人，依韶求仕，乃分屬諸將，或殺降羌老弱予以首為功級。

translations.literal: Shao's kin were mostly Chu men seeking office through him; he assigned them to generals, or killed old and weak surrendered Qiang and presented heads for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chu kin sought office through him; he assigned them to generals or killed weak Qiang for merit heads.

sentences.zh: 韶晚節言動不常，頗若病狂狀。

translations.literal: In his late years words and acts were irregular, rather like madness.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life his words and acts were irregular, like madness.

sentences.zh: 既病疽，洞見五髒，蓋亦多殺徵云。

translations.literal: When the carbuncle came he saw his five organs through—perhaps because of excessive killing, it was said.
translations.idiomatic: When the carbuncle came he saw through his organs—perhaps from excessive killing.

sentences.zh: 子十人，厚、寀最顯。

translations.literal: He had ten sons; Hou and Cai were most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons; Hou and Cai were most prominent.

sentences.zh: 子 厚

translations.literal: Son Hou
translations.idiomatic: Son Hou

sentences.zh: 厚，字處道。

translations.literal: Hou, styled Chudao.
translations.idiomatic: Hou, styled Chudao.

sentences.zh: 少從父兵間，暢習羌事，官累通直郎。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father in campaigns, fluent in Qiang affairs, offices accumulating to Gentlemen for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: Young he followed his father in war, fluent in Qiang affairs, rising to Gentlemen for Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 元祐棄河、湟，厚上疏陳不可，且詣政事堂言之，不聽。

translations.literal: In Yuanyou when He and Huang were abandoned, Hou memorialized it could not be done and went to the council hall to say so; they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou when He and Huang were abandoned, Hou memorialized against it at the council hall; they would not listen.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，用薦者換禮賓副使、幹當熙河公事。

translations.literal: In Shaosheng through recommendation he was changed to vice commissioner of ritual guests and handled Xihe affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng he was made vice ritual commissioner handling Xihe.

sentences.zh: 會羌酋瞎征、隴拶爭國，河州守將王贍與厚同獻議復故地。

translations.literal: When Qiang chiefs Zhezheng and Longzan fought for power, He prefecture defender Wang Zhan and Hou together memorialized to recover old territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezheng and Longzan fought, Wang Zhan and Hou memorialized to recover old territory.

sentences.zh: 元符元年六月，師出塞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, sixth month, the army went beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu year one, sixth month, the army crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 七月，下邈川，降瞎征。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Moyuchuan was taken and Zhezheng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Moyuchuan fell and Zhezheng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 九月，次青唐，隴拶出迎。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they reached Qingtang and Longzan came out to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they reached Qingtang and Longzan welcomed them.

sentences.zh: 遂定湟、鄯。

translations.literal: Tao and Shan were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Tao and Shan were settled.

sentences.zh: 詔賜隴拶姓名曰趙懷德，進厚東上閤門副使、知湟州。

translations.literal: An edict gave Longzan the name Zhao Huaide; Hou was advanced to vice commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate and knew Tao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Longzan was named Zhao Huaide; Hou became Eastern Upper Gate vice commissioner and Tao prefect.

sentences.zh: 既而他種叛，合兵來攻，厚不能支。

translations.literal: Soon other tribes rebelled and combined to attack; Hou could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Soon other tribes rebelled; Hou could not hold.

sentences.zh: 朝廷度二州不可守，乃以畀懷德，而貶厚右內府率，再貶賀州別駕。

translations.literal: Court judged the two prefectures could not be held, gave them to Huaide, and demoted Hou to Right Inner Palace rate, then again to Hezhou army adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Court gave the prefectures to Huaide and demoted Hou to Inner Palace rate, then Hezhou adjutant.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，蔡京復開邊，還厚前秩，於是羌人多羅巴奉懷德之弟溪賒羅撒謀復國。

translations.literal: At the start of Chongning Cai Jing reopened the frontier and restored Hou's former rank; then many Duoluoba supported Huaide's brother Xisheluosha to restore the state.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongning Cai Jing restored Hou; Duoluoba backed Xisheluosha to restore the state.

sentences.zh: 懷德畏逼，奔河南，種落更挾之以令諸部。

translations.literal: Huaide feared pressure and fled to Henan; tribes again used him to command the departments.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide fled to Henan; tribes used him to command departments.

sentences.zh: 朝廷患眾羌扇結，命厚安撫洮西，遣內客省使童貫偕往。

translations.literal: Court feared Qiang stirring; ordered Hou to pacify Taoxi and sent palace envoy Tong Guan with him.
translations.idiomatic: Court ordered Hou to pacify Taoxi with Tong Guan.

sentences.zh: 多羅巴知王師且至，集眾以拒。

translations.literal: Duoluoba knew the royal army was coming and gathered crowds to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Duoluoba gathered crowds to resist.

sentences.zh: 厚聲言駐兵而陰戒行，羌備益弛，乃與偏將高永年異道出。

translations.literal: Hou proclaimed he would camp while secretly ordering the march; Qiang defenses relaxed; he and vice general Gao Yongnian took separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Hou proclaimed a halt while secretly marching; Qiang relaxed; he and Gao Yongnian split routes.

sentences.zh: 多羅巴三子以數萬人分據險，厚進擊破殺之，唯少子阿蒙中流矢去，道遇多羅巴，與俱遁。

translations.literal: Duoluoba's three sons held the defiles with tens of thousands; Hou advanced, broke and killed them; only the youngest A Meng was wounded and fled; on the road he met Duoluoba and both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Duoluoba's three sons held defiles; Hou broke them; only A Meng fled wounded and met Duoluoba escaping.

sentences.zh: 遂拔湟州。

translations.literal: Tao prefecture was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was taken.

sentences.zh: 以功進威州團練使、熙河經略安撫。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Wei training commissioner and Xihe commissioner pacifying.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was Wei training commissioner and Xihe pacifier.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，厚帥大軍次於湟，命永年將左軍循宗水而北，別將張誡將右軍出宗谷而南，自將中軍趨綏遠，期會宗哥川，羌置陳臨宗水，倚北山，溪賒羅撒張黃屋，建大旆，乘高指呼，望中軍旗鼓爭赴之。

translations.literal: In the third year, fourth month, Hou led the great army at Tao, ordered Yongnian's left along Zongshui north, Zhang Jie's right out Zong valley south, himself center toward Suiyuan, to meet at Zongge River. Qiang arrayed along Zongshui leaning on the north mountain; Xisheluosha raised a yellow canopy and great banner on high calling; seeing the center banner they rushed it.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, fourth month, Hou camped at Tao: Yongnian north on Zongshui, Zhang Jie south on Zong valley, Hou center to Suiyuan, meeting at Zongge. Qiang leaned on the north mountain; Xisheluosha called from high; they rushed the center.

sentences.zh: 厚麾遊騎登山攻其背，親帥強弩迎射，羌退走，右軍濟水擊之，大風從東南來，揚沙翳羌目，不得視，遂大敗，斬首四千三百餘級，俘三千餘人。

translations.literal: Hou sent skirmishers up the mountain on their rear and led strong crossbows; wind from the southeast raised sand blinding Qiang eyes; great defeat—four thousand three hundred beheaded, three thousand captured.
translations.idiomatic: Hou attacked their rear and shot strong crossbows; southeast wind blinded them; four thousand three hundred beheaded, three thousand captured.

sentences.zh: 羅撒以一騎馳去，其母龜茲公主與諸酋開鄯州降。

translations.literal: Luosha fled on one horse; his mother the Kucha princess and chiefs opened Shan and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Luosha fled; his mother the Kucha princess and chiefs opened Shan.

sentences.zh: 厚計羅撒必且走青唐，將夜追之，童貫以為不能及，遂止。

translations.literal: Hou judged Luosha would flee to Qingtang and wished to pursue by night; Guan thought it impossible and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hou wished to pursue Luosha by night; Guan stopped him.

sentences.zh: 師下青唐，知羅撒留一宿去，貫始悔之。

translations.literal: The army reached Qingtang; knowing Luosha had stayed one night and left, Guan then regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingtang Luosha had left overnight; Guan regretted it.

sentences.zh: 厚將大軍趣廓州，酋落施軍令結以眾降，遂入廓州。

translations.literal: Hou led the great army to Kuo; chieftain Shijunling submitted with his crowd; they entered Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Hou advanced to Kuo; Shijunling submitted; they entered Kuo.

sentences.zh: 超拜厚武勝軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to Wusheng military observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially made Wusheng observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，羅撒復入寇，永年戰死，羌焚大通河橋以叛，新疆大震。

translations.literal: The next year Luosha invaded again; Yongnian died in battle; Qiang burned the Datong bridge and rebelled; the new frontier was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Luosha invaded; Yongnian died; Qiang burned Datong bridge; the frontier shook.

sentences.zh: 厚坐逗遛，降郢州防禦使。

translations.literal: Hou was punished for delay and demoted to Ezhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hou was demoted to Ezhou defense commissioner for delay.

sentences.zh: 已而趙懷德約降未決，厚以書諭之，懷德即納款。

translations.literal: Zhao Huaide's surrender was undecided; Hou wrote to persuade him and Huaide submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide's surrender wavered; Hou persuaded him and he submitted.

sentences.zh: 還厚舊官。

translations.literal: Hou's former office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Hou's office was restored.

sentences.zh: 入朝，提舉醴泉觀，卒。

translations.literal: Entering court he directed the Liquan palace and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court, directed Liquan palace, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈寧遠軍節度使，諡曰「莊敏」。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Ningyuan military commissioner with posthumous name "Zhuangmin."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Ningyuan military commissioner, posthumous name "Zhuangmin."

sentences.zh: 子 寀

translations.literal: Son Cai
translations.idiomatic: Son Cai

sentences.zh: 寀，字輔道。

translations.literal: Cai, styled Fudao.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, styled Fudao.

sentences.zh: 好學，工詞章。

translations.literal: Fond of learning, skilled in lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was skilled in lyrics.

sentences.zh: 登第，至校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations to collator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations to collator.

sentences.zh: 忽若有所睹，遂感心疾，唯好延道流談丹砂、神仙事。

translations.literal: Suddenly as if he saw something, he developed mental illness and only delighted in Daoists discussing cinnabar and immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he seemed to see something, developed mental illness, and only talked with Daoists about immortals.

sentences.zh: 得鄭州書生，託左道，自言天神可祈而下，下則聲容與人接。

translations.literal: He obtained a Zhengzhou scholar who practiced left-hand arts, claiming the heavenly spirit could be prayed down; when down its voice and face met people.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhengzhou scholar practiced occult arts, claiming spirits could be summoned with human voice and face.

sentences.zh: 因習行其術，才能什七八，須兩人共為乃驗。

translations.literal: He practiced the art and could manage seven or eight tenths; it required two people together to work.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced the art at seven or eight tenths efficacy, needing two people together.

sentences.zh: 外間讙傳，浸淫徹禁庭。

translations.literal: Outside it spread in clamor until it reached the forbidden palace.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread until they reached the forbidden palace.

sentences.zh: 徽宗方崇道教，侍晨林靈素自度技不如，願與之遊，拒弗許。

translations.literal: Huizong was then exalting Daoism; attendant Lin Lingsu measured his skill as inferior and wished to associate with Cai but was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong exalted Daoism; Lin Lingsu wished to join Cai but was refused.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書劉昺，寀外兄也，久以爭進絕還往，神降寀家，使因昺以達，寀言其故，神曰：「第往與之言，汝某年月日在蔡京後堂談某事，有之否？」

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Liu Bing, Cai's cousin by marriage, long estranged over competing for advancement—the spirit descended at Cai's house and had him reach Bing through Bing; Cai told the reason; the spirit said: "Just go speak with him—were you not on such-and-such day in Cai Jing's rear hall discussing such-and-such, yes or no?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing, Cai's cousin, was estranged. The "spirit" told Cai to reach Bing and named secret slanders Bing had made in Cai Jing's hall.

sentences.zh: 昺驚駭汗洽，不能對，蓋所言皆陰中傷人者。

translations.literal: Bing was shocked, sweating, unable to answer—for all were secret injuries to people.
translations.idiomatic: Bing sweated, unable to answer—all were secret slanders.

sentences.zh: 乃言之帝，即召。

translations.literal: He then told the emperor, who immediately summoned Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, who summoned Cai.

sentences.zh: 寀風儀既高，又善談論，應對合上指。

translations.literal: Cai's bearing was high and he spoke well; his answers fit the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Cai bore himself well and answered to the emperor's liking.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，約某日即內殿致天神。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and set a day to summon the spirit in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set a day to summon the spirit in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 靈素求與共事，又弗許。

translations.literal: Lingsu again asked to share the work and was again refused.
translations.idiomatic: Lingsu again asked to share and was refused.

sentences.zh: 或謂靈素，但勿令鄭書生偕，寀當立敗。

translations.literal: Some told Lingsu: only do not let the Zhengzhou scholar accompany him and Cai will fail at once.
translations.idiomatic: Some told Lingsu: keep the Zhengzhou scholar out and Cai will fail.

sentences.zh: 即白帝曰：「寀父兄昔在西邊，密與夏人謀反國。

translations.literal: He told the emperor: "Cai's father and brothers once on the western border secretly plotted rebellion with the Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor: "Cai's kin once plotted with the Xia on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遲至尊候神，且圖不軌。」

translations.literal: Wait for the emperor to await the spirit and they will plot treachery."
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty awaits the spirit they will plot treachery."

sentences.zh: 帝疑焉。

translations.literal: The emperor grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 及是日，寀與書生至東華門，靈素戒閽卒獨聽寀入。

translations.literal: On that day Cai and the scholar reached the Eastern Glory Gate; Lingsu warned the gate guards to admit only Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Cai and the scholar reached Eastern Glory Gate; Lingsu admitted only Cai.

sentences.zh: 帝齋潔敬待，越三夕無所聞，乃下寀大理，獄成，棄市，昺竄瓊州。

translations.literal: The emperor fasted and waited; after three nights nothing was heard; Cai was sent to the grand court, the case fixed, executed in the market; Bing was exiled to Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: After three nights nothing came; Cai was tried, executed; Bing exiled to Qiong.

sentences.zh: 薛向，字師正。

translations.literal: Xue Xiang, styled Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiang, styled Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 以祖顏任太廟齋郎，為永壽主簿，權京兆戶曹。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather Yan he served as temple attendant and was Yongshou registrar, acting Jingzhao household officer.
translations.idiomatic: Through his grandfather Yan he was temple attendant, Yongshou registrar, acting Jingzhao household officer.

sentences.zh: 有商胡齎銀二篋，出樞密使王德用書，云以與其弟。

translations.literal: A merchant Hu carried two chests of silver with a letter from Military Affairs commissioner Wang Deyong saying it was for his brother.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant carried silver with Wang Deyong's letter for his brother.

sentences.zh: 向適監稅，疑之曰：「烏有大臣寄家問而諉胡人者？」

translations.literal: Xiang was supervising tax and suspected: "How can a great minister send family letters through a Hu?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang supervising tax asked: "How can a minister send family letters through a Hu?"

sentences.zh: 鞫之，果妄。

translations.literal: He interrogated; it was indeed false.
translations.idiomatic: He interrogated; it was false.

sentences.zh: 為邠州司法參軍。

translations.literal: He was made judicial officer of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He was Bin judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 夏人叛，秦中治城，侍御史陳洎行邊，向詣洎陳三敝，言：「今板築暴興，吏持斧四出伐木，無問井閭丘隴，民不敢訴。

translations.literal: When the Xia rebelled Qin was building walls; investigating censor Chen Ji toured the border; Xiang told Ji three abuses, saying: "Now plank building rises suddenly; clerks with axes cut trees everywhere regardless of wells, lanes, mounds—people dare not complain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia rebelled and Qin built walls, investigating censor Chen Ji toured the border, and Xiang told Ji of three abuses, saying: "Now plank building rises suddenly; clerks with axes cut trees everywhere regardless of wells, lanes, and mounds—people dare not complain.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，宜且葺邊城。

translations.literal: If it must be done, repair only the border forts.
translations.idiomatic: If it must be done, repair only border forts.

sentences.zh: 函關，秦東塞，今西向設守，是為棄關內乎？

translations.literal: Hangu Pass is Qin's eastern barrier; now guards face west—is this abandoning the interior?
translations.idiomatic: Hangu Pass is Qin's eastern barrier; guards now face west—is that abandoning the interior?

sentences.zh: 三司貸龍門富人錢，以百年全盛之天下，一方有警，即稱貸於民，非義也。」

translations.literal: The Three Departments lend Longmen rich men money—a century of prosperity and one alarm and they borrow from the people—is not righteous."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments borrow from Longmen rich men in one alarm—not righteous."

sentences.zh: 洎上其說，悉從之。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized; all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji memorialized; all were adopted.

sentences.zh: 邠守貪遝，欲因事為邪，並治於城，立表於市以撤屋，冀得賂免，向力爭罷之。

translations.literal: The Bin prefect was greedy and wished to use the matter for evil, together building at the city, erecting a placard in the market to tear down houses hoping for bribes to escape; Xiang struggled and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The Bin prefect was greedy; Xiang stopped his abuse of wall-building.

sentences.zh: 監在京榷貨務，連歲羨緡錢，當遷秩，移與其兄。

translations.literal: Supervising metropolitan commodity trade, surplus cash yearly should have meant promotion; he transferred it to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising commodity trade with yearly surplus, he gave promotion credit to his brother.

sentences.zh: 三司判官董沔議改河北便糴，行鈔法。

translations.literal: Three Departments judge Dong Mian debated changing Hebei convenience grain transport to paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Mian debated Hebei convenience grain and paper notes.

sentences.zh: 向曰：「如此，則都內之錢不繼，茶、鹽、香、象將益不售矣。」

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Thus capital money will not flow; tea, salt, incense, and ivory will sell even less."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: "Capital money will not flow; tea, salt, and ivory will sell less."

sentences.zh: 有司主沔議，既而邊糴滯不行，沔坐黜。

translations.literal: The office backed Mian; then border grain stalled and Mian was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The office backed Mian; border grain stalled; Mian was demoted.

sentences.zh: 以向知鄜州。

translations.literal: Xiang was made Yan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was made Yan prefect.

sentences.zh: 大水冒城郭，沉室廬，死者相枕。

translations.literal: Great flood covered the city, sank houses; the dead lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Flood covered the city; the dead lay in heaps.

sentences.zh: 郡卒戍延安，詣主將求歸視弗得，皆亡奔。

translations.literal: Commandery troops garrisoned Yan'an, asked the commander to return home to look and were refused; all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Troops at Yan'an begged to return home, were refused, and fled.

sentences.zh: 至，則家人無存者，聚謀為盜，民大恐。

translations.literal: Arriving, their families were gone; they gathered to plot banditry; the people were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Families were gone; they plotted banditry; people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 向遣吏曉之曰：「冒法以赴急，人之常情，而不聽若輩歸，此武將不知變之過也。

translations.literal: Xiang sent clerks to explain: "Breaking law for urgent family need is human feeling; not hearing you return is the martial officer's fault not knowing change.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang explained: "Urgent family need is human; refusing return is the commander's fault.

sentences.zh: 亟往收溺屍，貰汝擅還之罪。」

translations.literal: Hurry to collect drowned bodies and I pardon your unauthorized return."
translations.idiomatic: Collect the drowned and I pardon your unauthorized return."

sentences.zh: 眾入庭下泣謝，一境乃安。

translations.literal: The crowd came below the hall weeping thanks; the whole district was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They wept thanks; the district was pacified.

sentences.zh: 又論河北糴法之弊，以為：「度支歲費錢緡五百萬，所得半直，其贏皆入賈販家。

translations.literal: He also debated abuses of Hebei grain purchase, saying: "The fiscal branch yearly spends five million strings, getting half value; profit all enters merchant houses.
translations.idiomatic: He also debated abuses of Hebei grain purchase, saying: "The fiscal branch spends five million strings yearly, getting half value; profit all goes to merchant houses.

sentences.zh: 今當有以權之，遇穀貴，則官糴於澶，魏，載以給邊；

translations.literal: Now there should be weight: when grain is dear, the office buys at Cao and Wei and ships to the border;
translations.idiomatic: When grain is dear, buy at Cao and Wei for the border;

sentences.zh: 新陳未交，則散糴價以救民乏；

translations.literal: when old and new grain have not met, scatter sale price to aid the people;
translations.idiomatic: when stocks turn, sell to aid the people;

sentences.zh: 軍食有餘，則坐倉收之。

translations.literal: when army food is surplus, store in granaries.
translations.idiomatic: when surplus, store in granaries.

sentences.zh: 此策一行，穀將不可勝食矣。」

translations.literal: Once this policy runs, grain will be more than can be eaten."
translations.idiomatic: Once this policy runs, grain will be inexhaustible."

sentences.zh: 朝廷是向計，始置便糴司於大名，以向為提點刑獄兼其事。

translations.literal: Court approved Xiang's plan and first established the convenience grain office at Daming with Xiang as judicial commissioner concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Court approved; established convenience grain office at Daming with Xiang.

sentences.zh: 武強有盜殺人而逸，尉捕平民抑使承，向覆其冤，脫六囚於死。

translations.literal: At Wuqiang a thief killed a man and fled; the sheriff seized a commoner and forced confession; Xiang reversed the injustice and freed six from death.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuqiang Xiang reversed a false confession and freed six from death.

sentences.zh: 入為開封度支判官，權陝西轉運副使、制置解鹽。

translations.literal: He entered as Kaifeng revenue judge, acting Shaanxi vice transport commissioner and director of Jie salt.
translations.idiomatic: He became Kaifeng revenue judge, acting Shaanxi vice transport commissioner, director of Jie salt.

sentences.zh: 鹽足支十年，而歲調畦夫數千，向奏損其數。

translations.literal: Salt sufficed for ten years yet thousands of saltern workers were levied yearly; Xiang memorialized to reduce the number.
translations.idiomatic: Salt lasted ten years yet thousands of workers were levied; Xiang reduced the number.

sentences.zh: 兼提舉買馬，監牧沙苑養馬，歲得駒三百，而費錢四千萬，占田千頃。

translations.literal: He also directed horse purchase; pasture at Shayuan raised horses, yearly three hundred foals at forty million cash and a thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: He directed horse purchase; Shayuan cost forty million and a thousand qing yearly.

sentences.zh: 向請斥閑田予民，收租入以市之。

translations.literal: Xiang asked to give idle land to the people and use rent to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang gave idle land to people and used rent to buy horses.

sentences.zh: 乃置場於原、渭，以羨鹽之直市馬，於是馬一歲至萬匹。

translations.literal: He established a market at Yuan and Wei using surplus salt value to buy horses; thus ten thousand horses a year.
translations.idiomatic: He used surplus salt at Yuan and Wei to buy ten thousand horses a year.

sentences.zh: 昭陵復土，計用錢糧五十萬貫石，三司不能供億，將移陝西緣邊入鹽中於永安縣。

translations.literal: Zhaoling earth restoration needed five hundred thousand strings and stone; the Three Departments could not supply and would move Shaanxi border salt into Yongan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoling restoration needed five hundred thousand; Three Departments would move border salt to Yongan.

sentences.zh: 向陳五不可，以為失信商旅，遂舉所闕之數以獻。

translations.literal: Xiang cited five impossibilities, saying it would break faith with merchants, and offered the shortfall himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang cited five impossibilities and offered the shortfall himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜至靈寶縣，先驅入驛，與客崔令孫爭舍。

translations.literal: Once at night he reached Lingbao; his outrider entered the post station and contested quarters with the guest Cui Lingsun.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingbao his outrider fought Cui Lingsun for quarters.

sentences.zh: 令孫正病臥，驚而死，罷知汝州。

translations.literal: Lingsun was ill in bed, startled and died; Xiang was dismissed to Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Lingsun died of fright; Xiang was dismissed to Ru.

sentences.zh: 甫數月，復以為陝西轉運副使，進為使。

translations.literal: Barely months later he was again Shaanxi vice transport commissioner and promoted commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was again Shaanxi vice commissioner, then commissioner.

sentences.zh: 厚陵役費，其助如永昭時，凡將漕八年，所入鹽、馬、芻、粟數累萬，民不益賦，其課為最。

translations.literal: Thick tomb labor costs matched Yongzhao; in eight years as transport commissioner salt, horses, fodder, and grain totaled tens of thousands; the people were not additionally taxed; his rating was highest.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years as commissioner he supplied salt, horses, and grain without extra taxes—highest rating.

sentences.zh: 夏將嵬名山以綏州來歸，青澗城主种諤將往迎，詔向與議。

translations.literal: Xia general Wei Mingshan came to submit Sui prefecture; Zhong E of Qingjian wished to go welcome; an edict ordered Xiang to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingshan submitted Sui; Zhong E wished to welcome; Xiang was ordered to discuss.

sentences.zh: 諤不俟命，亟率所部出塞，遂城之。

translations.literal: E did not await orders and urgently led his troops beyond the border and fortified it.
translations.idiomatic: E did not await orders, crossed the border, and fortified.

sentences.zh: 廷議劾諤擅興，將致法。

translations.literal: Court debated impeaching E for unauthorized action and would punish by law.
translations.idiomatic: Court impeached E for unauthorized action.

sentences.zh: 向言：「諤今者之舉，蓋忘身以徇國，有如不稱，臣請坐之。」

translations.literal: Xiang said: "E's act today forgets body to serve the state; if it fails, your servant asks to bear the guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: "E forgets himself for the state; if it fails, punish me."

sentences.zh: 諤既貶，向亦罷知絳州，再貶信州，移潞州。

translations.literal: E was demoted and Xiang was dismissed to Jiang, again demoted to Xin, moved to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: E was demoted; Xiang to Jiang, Xin, then Lu.

sentences.zh: 張靖使陝西還，陳向制置鹽、馬之失。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing returned from Shaanxi and reported Xiang's failures in salt and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing reported Xiang's salt and horse failures.

sentences.zh: 詔向詣闕與辯，靖辭窮，即罪之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xiang to court to debate; Jing was speechless and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang debated at court; Jing was punished.

sentences.zh: 神宗知向材，以為江、浙、荊、淮發運使。

translations.literal: Shenzong knew Xiang's talent and made him transport commissioner of Jiang, Zhe, Jing, and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong made him transport commissioner of Jiang, Zhe, Jing, and Huai.

sentences.zh: 綱舟曆歲久，篙工利於盜貨，嘗假風水沉溺以滅跡。

translations.literal: Canal boats aged yearly; boatmen profited by theft and often feigned wind and water sinking to hide traces.
translations.idiomatic: Canal boats aged; boatmen stole and sank boats to hide traces.

sentences.zh: 向募客舟分載，以相督察。

translations.literal: Xiang hired passenger boats to divide loads for mutual oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang hired passenger boats to divide loads for oversight.

sentences.zh: 官舟有定數，多為主者冒占，悉奪畀屬州，諸運皆詣本曹受遣；

translations.literal: Official boats had fixed numbers often falsely claimed; he took all and gave to commanderies; all transport went to original offices for dispatch;
translations.idiomatic: He ended false boat claims and returned dispatch to commanderies;

sentences.zh: 以地有美惡，利有重輕，為立等式，用所漕物為誅賞。

translations.literal: because land had good and bad and profit heavy and light, he made grades and used transported goods for reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: he graded land and used cargo for rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 遷天章閣待制。

translations.literal: He was moved to Heavenly Manifest attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Heavenly Manifest attendant.

sentences.zh: 環慶有疆事，帝以向習知地形，召詣中書。

translations.literal: Huan and Qing had border affairs; the emperor knew Xiang understood terrain and summoned him to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huan and Qing had border trouble; the emperor summoned Xiang to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 舊制，發運使上計，毋得出入，唯止都門達章奏。

translations.literal: Old rule: transport commissioners on accounting might not enter or leave—only reach the capital gate with memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Old rule barred transport commissioners from entering the capital except with memorials.

sentences.zh: 至是，弛其禁。

translations.literal: Now that restriction was relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: That restriction was relaxed.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，權三司使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining he acted as Three Departments commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining year four he acted Three Departments commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明堂禮成，有司誤遷向右諫議大夫，詔罰吏而向官不奪。

translations.literal: After Bright Hall rites an office mistakenly moved him to Right Remonstrator; an edict punished clerks but did not strip Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Bright Hall rites clerks mistakenly promoted him; clerks were punished, not Xiang.

sentences.zh: 河、洮用兵，縣官費不可計，向未嘗乏供給。

translations.literal: He and Tao campaigns cost uncountable funds; Xiang never lacked supply.
translations.idiomatic: He and Tao campaigns cost uncountably; Xiang never lacked supply.

sentences.zh: 及解嚴，上疏乞戒將帥裁溢員，汰冗卒、省浮費、節橫賦，手敕褒納。

translations.literal: When war eased he memorialized to warn generals, cut surplus posts, eliminate redundant troops, reduce floating expense, restrain exactions; the emperor praised it by hand.
translations.idiomatic: When war eased he memorialized to cut waste; the emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to direct Dragon Diagram academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct Dragon Diagram academician.

sentences.zh: 遼人求代北地，北邊擇牧，加樞密直學士、給事中、知定州。

translations.literal: Liao sought northern territory; the north chose pasture; he was made bureau direct academician, giving access, and Ding prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Liao sought northern land; he was bureau academician and Ding prefect.

sentences.zh: 高陽關募兵，敵陰遣人應選。

translations.literal: Gaoyang Pass recruited troops; the enemy secretly sent men to enlist.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyang Pass recruited; the enemy secretly sent men.

sentences.zh: 向諜知之，主者覺，縱使亡去，向遣邏捕取之，械送瀛州，戮於市。

translations.literal: Xiang learned it; the recruiter noticed, let them flee; Xiang sent patrols to seize and send them in irons to Ying, executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang learned it; patrols seized them and executed them at Ying.

sentences.zh: 北使久留都亭，數出不遜語，而雲、應點兵，涿、易治道，僉謂必諭盟。

translations.literal: Northern envoys long stayed at Duting, often spoke insolently; Yun and Ying massed troops; Zhuo and Yi repaired roads—all said the alliance was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Northern envoys were insolent; troops massed; all said the alliance was broken.

sentences.zh: 向曰：「彼欲疆議速成，故多張虛勢以撼我。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "They wish the border talks to succeed quickly, so they multiply empty show to shake us.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: "They want quick success, so they bluff.

sentences.zh: 使者懼不如其請，故肆嫚言以徼幸取成。

translations.literal: The envoys fear their request will not be granted, so they speak rudely to gamble for success.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys fear refusal, so they speak rudely to gamble.

sentences.zh: 兵來不除道，其亦無能為也已。」

translations.literal: Troops come yet do not repair roads—they also can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Troops come but do not repair roads—they can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 後皆如向言。

translations.literal: Later all was as Xiang said.
translations.idiomatic: Later all was as Xiang said.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 向控辭，賜詔弗允。

translations.literal: Xiang declined; the emperor granted edict not permitting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang declined; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 故事，前兩府辭官乃降詔，兩省得詔自向始。

translations.literal: Story: only the two councils declined with edict; both ministries receiving edict began with Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Only the two councils had decline edicts; both ministries began with Xiang.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，召同知樞密院。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng he was summoned as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng year one he was vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 向幹局絕人，尤善商財，計算無遺策，用心至到，然甚者不能無病民，所上課間失實。

translations.literal: Xiang's capacity was unmatched, especially skilled at merchant wealth and calculation without missed strategy, utmost care—yet at the extreme he could not avoid harming the people; submitted ratings sometimes lacked truth.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's capacity was unmatched in finance and calculation, yet at extremes he harmed people; ratings sometimes lied.

sentences.zh: 時方尚功利，王安石從中主之，御史數有言，不聽也。

translations.literal: The time exalted merit; Wang Anshi backed him from within; censors often spoke; they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was exalted; Anshi backed him; censors spoke in vain.

sentences.zh: 向以是益得展奮其材業，至於論兵帝所，通暢明決，遂由文俗吏得大用。

translations.literal: Xiang thus could expand his enterprise; discussing war before the emperor he was clear and decisive—from civil clerk to great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xiang expanded; discussing war he was clear—from civil clerk to great use.

sentences.zh: 及在政地，同列質以西北事，則養威持重，未嘗啟其端，非常所以屬望意。

translations.literal: In power, colleagues asked about the northwest; he nurtured prestige and held weight, never opening the matter—not what was usually hoped.
translations.idiomatic: In power he held weight on the northwest and never opened the matter—not what was hoped.

sentences.zh: 會詔民畜馬，向既奉命，旋知民不便，議欲改為。

translations.literal: When the edict ordered the people to raise horses, Xiang had just received command and knew the people were troubled; he debated changing it.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to raise horses, Xiang knew the people suffered and debated change.

sentences.zh: 於是舒亶論向反覆無大臣體，斥知潁州。

translations.literal: Then Shu Dan attacked Xiang for reversal without a great minister's body and expelled him to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Dan attacked his reversal and expelled him to Ying.

sentences.zh: 又改隨州，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Again changed to Sui; he died at sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Sui and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，錄其言，諡曰「恭敏」。

translations.literal: In Yuanyou his words were recorded; posthumous name "Gongmin."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou his words were recorded; posthumous name "Gongmin."

sentences.zh: 子紹彭，有翰墨名，中子嗣昌。

translations.literal: Son Shaopeng had fame in calligraphy; middle son Sichang.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shaopeng was famed in calligraphy; middle son Sichang.

sentences.zh: 子 嗣昌

translations.literal: Son Sichang
translations.idiomatic: Son Sichang

sentences.zh: 嗣昌亦以吏材奮。

translations.literal: Sichang also rose through clerical talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang also rose through clerical talent.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，歷熙河轉運判官，梓州、陝西轉運副使，直龍圖閣、集賢殿修撰，入為左司郎中，擢徽猷閣待制、陝西都轉運使，知渭州，改慶州。

translations.literal: In Chongning he was Xihe transport judge, Zi prefecture and Shaanxi vice transport, Dragon Diagram academician, Left Department gentleman, Huizhou attendant, Shaanxi transport commissioner, Wei and Qing prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning he held Xihe, Zi, Shaanxi transport, Wei, and Qing posts.

sentences.zh: 監公使庫皇寘坐獄，嗣昌奏請之。

translations.literal: Supervisor Huang Zhen sat in prison; Sichang memorialized for him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Huang Zhen was imprisoned; Sichang memorialized for him.

sentences.zh: 遂以監臨自盜責安化軍節度副使，安置郢州。

translations.literal: Thus for supervising theft he was demoted to Anhua vice commissioner and settled at E.
translations.idiomatic: For supervising theft he was demoted to Anhua vice commissioner at E.

sentences.zh: 起知相州，復待制、知太原府。

translations.literal: Restored to Xiang prefecture, again attendant and Taiyuan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to Xiang, then attendant and Taiyuan prefect.

sentences.zh: 論築涇原三倉勞，加顯謨閣直學士；

translations.literal: Memorializing the labor of Jingyuan three granaries, he gained Exalted Scheme direct academician;
translations.idiomatic: Memorializing Jingyuan granaries he gained Exalted Scheme academician;

sentences.zh: 又以撫納西羌功，進延康、宣和殿學士，拜禮部、刑部尚書。

translations.literal: again for pacifying western Qiang, Yanhe and Xuanhe academics, Minister of Rites and Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: for pacifying Qiang he gained Yanhe and Xuanhe academics and both ministries.

sentences.zh: 坐啟擬反覆罷，提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Impeached for contradictory proposals and dismissed; director of Chongfu palace.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached for contradiction; director of Chongfu palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷延康殿學士、知延安府，賜第京師。

translations.literal: After long time Yanan academician and Yan'an prefect, granted capital residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yanan academician and Yan'an prefect with capital residence.

sentences.zh: 當遷官，丐回授其子昶京秩。

translations.literal: When he should be promoted he begged transfer to his son Chang for capital rank.
translations.idiomatic: He begged promotion credit for his son Chang.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌前後因事六七貶，多以欺罔獲罪。

translations.literal: Sichang was demoted six or seven times for deception.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang was demoted six or seven times for deception.

sentences.zh: 至是，言者並論之，降為待制，卒。

translations.literal: Now critics joined attack; he was demoted to attendant and died.
translations.idiomatic: Critics joined; he was demoted to attendant and died.

sentences.zh: 先是，徽宗有意圖北方，遣譚稹銜命訪諸帥，韓粹彥、洪中孚皆力云不可，嗣昌乃潤飾諜詞，以開邊隙。

translations.literal: Earlier Huizong wished to plot the north and sent Tan Ji to visit commanders; Han Cuiyan and Hong Zhongfu strongly said no; Sichang embellished spy words to open the border.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong wished to plot the north; Han and Hong refused; Sichang embellished spies to open war.

sentences.zh: 及論事帝前，語至興師，或感激流涕。

translations.literal: Before the emperor discussing affairs, speaking of raising troops he sometimes wept.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor on war he sometimes wept.

sentences.zh: 造亂之咎，人皆歸責焉。

translations.literal: The blame for making chaos all fell on him.
translations.idiomatic: Blame for chaos fell on him.

sentences.zh: 章楶，字質夫，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jie, styled Zhifu, was a man of Pucheng in Jian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie, styled Zhifu, was from Pucheng in Jian.

sentences.zh: 祖頻，為侍御史，忤章獻后旨黜官，仁宗欲用之而卒，楶以叔得象蔭，為孟州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pin was investigating censor, offended Empress Zhangxian and was demoted; Renzong wished to use him but he died; Jie through his uncle gained Xiang's yin and was Mengzhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Pin offended Empress Zhangxian; Jie gained yin and was Mengzhou registrar.

sentences.zh: 應舉入京，聞父對獄於魏，棄不就試，馳往直其冤。

translations.literal: Going to the capital for examination he heard his father was tried in Wei, abandoned the exam, raced to vindicate him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his father was tried in Wei, he abandoned the exam to vindicate him.

sentences.zh: 還，試禮部第一，擢知陳留縣，歷提舉陝西常平、京東轉運判官、提點湖北刑獄、成都路轉運使，入為考功、吏部、右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Returning he took first in the Ministry of Rites, was Chenliu magistrate, Shaanxi constant transport, Jingdong vice transport, Hubei judicial commissioner, Chengdu transport, entered as evaluation, personnel, and right department outside gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, he placed first in the Ministry of Rites examination, was promoted to magistrate of Chenliu, and successively served as supervisor of Shaanxi Ever-Normal Granaries, assistant fiscal commissioner for Jingdong, judicial intendant for Hubei, fiscal commissioner for Chengdu Circuit, and then entered court as junior vice director in the Bureaus of Merit Evaluation, Personnel, and the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，以直龍圖閣知慶州。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyou he was Dragon Diagram attendant and Qing prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanyou start he was Dragon Diagram attendant and Qing prefect.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷戢兵，戒邊吏勿妄動，且捐葭蘆、安疆等四砦予夏，使歸其永樂之人。

translations.literal: The court wished to cease arms and warned border officials not to act rashly; Jialu, Anjiang, and four other garrisons were given to Xia so Yongle people could return.
translations.idiomatic: Court ceased arms and gave four garrisons to Xia for Yongle people.

sentences.zh: 夏得砦益驕。

translations.literal: The Xia grew more arrogant with the garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia grew more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 楶言：「夏嗜利畏威，不有懲艾，邊不得休息，宜稍取其土疆，如古削地之制，以固吾圉。

translations.literal: Jie said: "The Xia covet profit and fear might; without punishment the border cannot rest; take some territory as ancient land-cutting to secure our defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said: "Without punishment the border cannot rest; cut some territory as ancient custom.

sentences.zh: 然後諸路出兵，據其要害，不一再舉，勢將自蹙矣。」

translations.literal: Then various routes send troops, hold key points—once or twice and they will be pressed."
translations.idiomatic: Then routes send troops on key points—once or twice they will be pressed."

sentences.zh: 遂乘便出討，以致其師，夏果入圍環州。

translations.literal: He took opportunity to campaign and provoke them; the Xia indeed entered and besieged Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He provoked them; the Xia besieged Huan.

sentences.zh: 楶先用間知之，遣驍將折可適伏兵洪德城。

translations.literal: Jie first knew by spy, sent the brave Zhe Keshi to ambush at Hongde city.
translations.idiomatic: Jie sent Zhe Keshi to ambush at Hongde.

sentences.zh: 夏師過之，伏兵識其母梁氏旗幟，鼓噪而出，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Xia army passed they knew Lady Liang's banners, shouted and rushed out, beheading and capturing greatly.
translations.idiomatic: They recognized Lady Liang's banners and struck greatly.

sentences.zh: 又預毒於牛圈瀦水，夏人馬飲者多死。

translations.literal: He also poisoned cattle pens and pooled water; many Xia horses died drinking.
translations.idiomatic: He poisoned water; many Xia horses died.

sentences.zh: 召權戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned acting Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned acting Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年，除知同州。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Tong prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was Tong prefect.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，知應天府，加集賢殿修撰、知廣州，徙江、淮發運使。

translations.literal: At the start of Shaosheng he knew Yingtian, gained Assembled Worthies academician and Guang prefect, moved to Jiang-Huai transport.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaosheng he knew Yingtian, Guang, and Jiang-Huai transport.

sentences.zh: 哲宗訪以邊事，對合旨，命知渭州。

translations.literal: Zhezong asked border affairs; his answer fit intent; he was ordered to know Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong asked border affairs; he was ordered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 至即上言城胡蘆河川，據形勝以逼夏。

translations.literal: Arriving he memorialized to fortify Hulu River valley and press Xia by terrain.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to fortify Hulu valley and press the Xia.

sentences.zh: 乃以三月及熙河、秦風、環慶四路之師，陽繕理他堡壁數十所，自示其怯。

translations.literal: In the third month with Xihe, Qinfeng, Huanqing four routes he feigned repairing dozens of other forts, showing fear.
translations.idiomatic: With four routes he feigned repairing other forts, showing fear.

sentences.zh: 或以楶怯，請曰：「此夏必爭之地，夏方營石門峽，去我三十里，能奪而有之乎？」

translations.literal: Some, saying he was timid, asked: "This is ground the Xia must contest; they are fortifying Shimen gorge thirty li from us—can we seize it?"
translations.idiomatic: Some, saying he was timid, asked: "This is ground the Xia must contest; they are fortifying Shimen gorge thirty li from us—can we seize it?"

sentences.zh: 楶又陽謝之，陰具板築守戰之備，帥四路師出胡蘆河川，築二城於石門峽江口好水河之陰。

translations.literal: Jie again outwardly declined but secretly prepared plank defense; he led four routes out Hulu valley and built two cities at Shimen gorge and Haoshui River.
translations.idiomatic: Jie secretly prepared and built two cities at Shimen and Haoshui.

sentences.zh: 二旬有二日成，賜名平夏城、靈平砦。

translations.literal: In twenty-two days they were done, named Pingxia city and Lingping garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In twenty-two days: Pingxia city and Lingping garrison.

sentences.zh: 方興役時，夏以其眾來乘，楶迎擊敗之。

translations.literal: During work the Xia came; Jie met and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia came; Jie defeated them.

sentences.zh: 既而環慶、鄜延、河東、熙河皆相繼築城，進拓其境，夏人愕視不敢動。

translations.literal: Then Huanqing, Yanyan, Hedong, and Xihe all built cities and expanded territory; the Xia stared in shock and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: All circuits built cities; the Xia dared not move.

sentences.zh: 夏主遂奉其母合將數十萬兵圍平夏，疾攻十餘日，建高車臨城，填塹而進，不能克，一夕遁去。

translations.literal: The Xia lord with his mother led hundreds of thousands to besiege Pingxia, attacked ten-odd days, built high carts, filled moats, could not take it, fled in one night.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia lord besieged Pingxia ten days and fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 夏統軍嵬名阿埋、西壽監軍妹勒都逋皆勇悍善戰，楶諜其弛備，遣折可適、郭成輕騎夜襲，直入其帳執之，盡俘其家，虜馘三千餘、牛羊十萬，夏主震駭。

translations.literal: Xia commanders Wei Mingmai and Xishou monitor Meile Dutong were brave; Jie learned they were lax, sent Zhe Keshi and Guo Cheng by night, seized them in their tents, captured families, three thousand heads, a hundred thousand livestock; the Xia lord was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Jie seized Mingmai and Dutong by night; the Xia lord was shaken.

sentences.zh: 哲宗為御紫宸殿受賀，累擢楶樞密直學士、龍圖閣端明殿學士，進階大中大夫。

translations.literal: Zhezong received congratulations at Zichen Hall and repeatedly promoted Jie bureau academician and Bright Hall academician to grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong received congratulations and promoted Jie repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 楶在涇原四年，凡創州一、城砦九，薦拔偏裨，不間廝役，至於夏降人折可適、李忠傑、朱智用，咸受其馭。

translations.literal: Jie four years at Jingyuan created one prefecture, nine garrisons, recommended officers from servants, and Qiang submitters Zhe Keshi, Li Zhongjie, and Zhu Zhiyong all obeyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Four years at Jingyuan he created one prefecture and nine garrisons and commanded submitters.

sentences.zh: 夏自平夏之敗，不復能軍，屢請命乞和，哲宗亦為之寢兵。

translations.literal: After Pingxia defeat the Xia could not field armies and often begged peace; Zhezong also rested arms.
translations.idiomatic: After Pingxia the Xia begged peace; Zhezong rested arms.

sentences.zh: 楶立邊功，為西方最。

translations.literal: Jie stood on the frontier as the greatest of the west.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was the greatest frontier merit in the west.

sentences.zh: 時章惇用事，楶與惇同宗，其得興事，頗為世所疑。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun held power; Jie shared clan; people suspected his rise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun held power; Jie shared clan; people suspected him.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，請老，徙知河南。

translations.literal: Huizong took the throne; Jie begged old age and moved to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong came; Jie begged old age and went to Henan.

sentences.zh: 入見，留拜同知樞密院事，俾其子縡為開封推官以便養。

translations.literal: On audience he was kept as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; his son Xu was Kaifeng investigating officer for his support.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept vice bureau director; son Xu was Kaifeng officer for support.

sentences.zh: 逾年，力謝事罷，授資政殿學士、中太一宮使，未幾，卒。

translations.literal: After a year he forcefully resigned, given Assisting Governance academician and Central Grand Unity director; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he resigned, given Assisting Governance academician; soon he died.

sentences.zh: 徽宗悼之。

translations.literal: Huizong mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈右銀青光祿大夫，諡曰「莊簡」，賻恤甚厚。

translations.literal: Posthumously Right Silver-Glitter Grandee, posthumous name "Zhuangjian," generous condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Right Silver-Glitter Grandee, posthumous name "Zhuangjian," generous condolence.

sentences.zh: 楶七子：縡、綜、綡、綰、綖、縯、縝。

translations.literal: Jie had seven sons: Xu, Zong, Qi, Wan, Yan, Yan, Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Seven sons: Xu, Zong, Qi, Wan, Yan, Yan, Zhen.

sentences.zh: 縡、綡最知名。

translations.literal: Xu and Qi were most known.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Qi were best known.

sentences.zh: 縡繇推官為戶部員外郎、提點淮南東路刑獄、權知揚州兼提舉香鹽事。

translations.literal: Xu from investigating officer to Revenue outside gentleman, Huainan east judicial commissioner, acting Yangzhou with incense and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Xu held Revenue, judicial, and Yangzhou salt posts.

sentences.zh: 時方鑄崇寧大錢，令下，市區晝閉，人持錢買物，至日旰，皇皇無肯售。

translations.literal: When casting Chongning great coins was ordered the market closed by day; people held coins until evening with none willing to sell.
translations.idiomatic: Chongning great coins closed markets; no one would sell.

sentences.zh: 縡飾市易務致百貨，以小錢收之；

translations.literal: Xu stocked the market office with goods and collected them in small coins;
translations.idiomatic: Xu stocked the market office and collected small coins;

sentences.zh: 且檄倉吏糶米，以大錢予之，盡十日止，民心遂安。

translations.literal: and ordered granary clerks to sell rice paying in great coins for ten days; the people were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: sold rice for great coins ten days; people calmed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，新鈔法行，舊鈔盡廢，一時商賈束手，或自殺。

translations.literal: Soon new note law came; old notes all void; merchants at once helpless, some killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: New notes voided old ones; merchants despaired; some killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 縡得訴者所持舊鈔，為錢以千計者三十萬，上疏言鈔法誤民，請如約以示大信。

translations.literal: Xu took old notes from complainants, cash to three hundred thousand strings, memorialized the note law harmed people and asked fulfillment of promises for great faith.
translations.idiomatic: Xu memorialized note law harm and asked faith to promises.

sentences.zh: 上怒，罷縡，降兩官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, dismissed Xu, demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted Xu two ranks.

sentences.zh: 綡第進士，歷陝西轉運判官，入為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: Qi passed examinations, Shaanxi vice transport judge, entered as Revenue outside gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Qi passed exams, Shaanxi judge, Revenue outside gentleman.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎劉逵之妻，綡姊也。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat vice minister Liu Kui's wife was Qi's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui's wife was Qi's sister.

sentences.zh: 逵漸復元祐之政，綡多贊之。

translations.literal: Kui gradually restored Yuanyou policies; Qi much aided him.
translations.idiomatic: Kui restored Yuanyou policies; Qi aided him.

sentences.zh: 蔡京欲擠逵，且惎綡不附己，使其黨攻之，出綡湖州。

translations.literal: Cai Jing wished to oust Kui and hated Qi not attaching to him, had his faction attack and sent Qi to Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing ousted Kui and sent Qi to Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 論者不已，差主管西京崇福宮。

translations.literal: Critics continued; he was made director of Western Capital Chongfu palace.
translations.idiomatic: Critics continued; he directed Western Capital Chongfu palace.

sentences.zh: 綜歷通判常州，綰知丹徒縣，綖簽判西安州，縯簽判蘇州，楶孫茇承奉郎，藎監蘇州稅，俱列仕顯。

translations.literal: Zong was Chang vice prefect, Wan Dantu magistrate, Yan Xi'an signatory, Yan Suzhou signatory, Jie grandson Ba receptionist, Jian Suzhou tax—all prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Zong served as assistant prefect of Changzhou, Wan as magistrate of Dantu County, Yan as signatory judge of Xi'an Prefecture, and Yan as signatory judge of Suzhou; Jie's grandson Ba was Gentleman for Court Service, and Jian supervised the Suzhou taxes. All were listed among prominent officeholders.

sentences.zh: 及京復相，遂興制獄，傾章氏。

translations.literal: When Jing returned as chief minister he launched prosecutions and overturned the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing returned he prosecuted the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 綖居蘇州，或得私鑄錢數巨罌，京風言者誣綖與州人郁寶所鑄。

translations.literal: Yan at Suzhou obtained a huge jar of private coin; Jing had rumormongers accuse Yan and Prefect Yu Bao of casting.
translations.idiomatic: Yan found private coin; Jing accused Yan and Yu Bao of casting.

sentences.zh: 詔遣李孝壽、張茂直、沈畸、蕭服更往鞫之，連繫數百人，累月卒無實，獄多死者。

translations.literal: Edict sent Li Xiaoshou, Zhang Maozhi, Shen Qi, Xiao Fu to investigate; hundreds chained months with no truth; many died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators chained hundreds months; many died; no truth.

sentences.zh: 京大怒，別遣孫傑鞫之，傅致如章綖刺面配沙門島，追毀出身以來文字，除名勒停，籍入其家。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly angry, sent Sun Jie; framed Yan as if tattooed and exiled to Shaolin Island, destroyed all texts since youth, name struck, family registered; Xu to Taizhou, Zong to Xiuzhou, Qi to Wen, Wan to Yong, Yan to Yong, Ba to Chuzhou, Jian to Jun—all demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jie framed Yan; clan exiled and struck from office.

sentences.zh: 竄縡台州，綜秀州，綡溫州，綰睦州，縯永州，茇處州，藎均州，官司降罷除名者十餘人，時論冤之。

translations.literal: Xu to Taizhou, Zong Xiuzhou, Qi Wen, Wan Yong, Yan Yong, Ba Chuzhou, Jian Jun—more than ten struck from office; opinion held it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten were struck; opinion held it unjust.

sentences.zh: 孫傑擢龍圖閣直學士、知蘇州，張商英入相，始辨前獄，移綖常州，綡復朝奉郎、通判秀州。

translations.literal: Sun Jie promoted Dragon Diagram direct academician and Suzhou prefect; Zhang Shangying entered as chief minister and began to right the case, moved Yan to Chang, Qi restored court gentleman and Xiuzhou vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jie rose; Shangying righted the case partially.

sentences.zh: 頃之，綖改授內殿崇班，綡秘書省校書郎，遷戶部員外郎，出提點兩浙刑獄，以龍圖閣直學士知越州。

translations.literal: Soon Yan was changed to Inner Palace Chongban; Liang was Collator in the Palace Library, then promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, sent out as Judicial Intendant of the Two Zhe circuits, and, as Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, made prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yan was reassigned as Inner Palace Chongban; Liang became Collator in the Palace Library, was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, went out as Judicial Intendant of the Two Zhe circuits, and, as Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, was made prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 譚稹宣撫燕山，請綡為參謀，加右文殿修撰。

translations.literal: Tan Ji pacified Yanshan and asked Qi as staff; added Right Culture academician.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Ji asked Qi as staff; Right Culture academician.

sentences.zh: 金人破蔚州，背歸山後議，稹以錯置乖方罷。

translations.literal: Jurchens broke Weizhou; back-mountain plan failed; Ji dismissed for misplacement.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchens broke Weizhou; Ji was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 綡落職送吏部，會赦恩，上書告老，復龍圖閣直學士致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Qi lost office to Personnel; amnesty; memorialized old age; restored Dragon Diagram academician retired; died.
translations.idiomatic: Qi retired as Dragon Diagram academician and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：神宗奮英特之資，乘財力之富，銳然欲復河、湟，平靈、夏，而蔡挺、王韶、章楶輩起諸生，委褒衣，樹勳戎馬間。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Shenzong with outstanding talent and rich treasury sharply wished to recover He and Huang, pacify Ling and Xia; Ting, Shao, and Jie rose from students, cast off scholar robes, and set merit between saddle and spear.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Shenzong wished to recover He and Huang; Ting, Shao, and Jie rose from students to merit in war.

sentences.zh: 世非無材，顧上所趣尚磨厲奚如耳。

translations.literal: The age was not without talent—only what the ruler prized and sharpened mattered.
translations.idiomatic: Talent existed—only what the ruler prized mattered.

sentences.zh: 觀挺之治兵，韶之策敵，楶之制勝，亦一時良將。

translations.literal: Seeing Ting's training troops, Shao's plotting enemy, Jie's gaining victory—they were fine generals of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Ting trained troops, Shao plotted enemies, Jie won battles—fine generals.

sentences.zh: 薛向雖無三子勞，而董漕邊饟，不乏仰給，持重樞府，不啟事端，又其善也。

translations.literal: Though Xiang lacked the three sons' labor, directing transport and frontier grain he never lacked supply; holding weight at the bureau without opening trouble was also his good point.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang supplied the frontier and held the bureau without opening trouble—that was his good.

sentences.zh: 若厚之降隴拶、瞎征，取湟、鄯、廓州，功足繼韶。

translations.literal: If Hou's lowering Longzan and Zhezheng and taking Tao, Shan, and Kuo matched Shao's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Hou's recovery of Tao, Shan, and Kuo could match Shao.

sentences.zh: 而嗣昌造釁北伐，乃悖於向，可勝誅邪？

translations.literal: Yet Sichang made trouble with northern campaign—contrary to Xiang—can execution suffice?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sichang made northern trouble contrary to Xiang—execution would hardly suffice.

sentences.zh: 雖然，佳兵好還，道家所戒，卒之寀以左道殺，綖以鑄錢陷，此非其驗也與。

translations.literal: Still, fine troops love return—the Daoists warn; in the end Cai was killed for left-hand arts, Yan trapped for coining—is this not verification?
translations.idiomatic: Still, the Daoists warn that fine troops love return; Cai was executed, Yan ruined for coining—is that not proof?
